item.title: A Winner Classification for Rooted Partizan Edge Geography on Heterogeneous Bouquets of Cycles
item.description: arXiv:2610.40683v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider an undirected edge-traversal game on a finite bouquet of simple cycles. Each of two players controls a token, both tokens begin at the common root, and the players alternate traversing edges that have not been used by either token. A player with no legal move loses. We prove that the first player wins precisely when the number of cycles of odd edge-length is odd, without assuming equal cycle lengths. The proof uses a simultaneous induction on root and defense configurations, with an exact analysis of the forced race between two opened cycles. We also explain how the classification corresponds to a completed Lean 4 formalization of the underlying game on finite edge sets.
item.dc:creator: Adam Til\`epe

item.title: Sharp bounds, stability, and arithmetic fluctuations for induced pentagons
item.description: arXiv:2610.40691v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that every graph with $m>0$ edges contains at most $\frac{3}{2\sqrt{2}}(\frac{m}{5})^{5/2}$ induced pentagons. Equality holds precisely for balanced blow-ups of the Clebsch graph, together with isolated vertices. The bound and equality classification extend to arbitrary nonnegative vertex weights and to all graphons, including fractional graphons. Moreover, a deficit of $\varepsilon$ in the normalized ratio can be repaired by $O(\sqrt{\varepsilon}m)$ edge edits on the original vertex set, producing an exactly balanced Clebsch blow-up and isolates. The exponent $1/2$ is optimal. We further separate the linear cost of adjacency errors from the quadratic cost of class imbalance. This yields an arithmetic description of the finite-edge deficit and its explicit second-order term, with a uniform power-saving remainder. For each fixed integer $j$, the exact extremal count at $m=40k^2+j$ is eventually an integer coefficient polynomial in $k$, computable by a finite enumeration; we do not quantify its threshold of validity. The proof combines global variational conditions, an active-density bound, and an exact rational certificate on the $1,044$ graphs of order seven. A positive-slope identity permits a single rational reference density. An exact conditional span excludes triangles at equality, after which degree and codegree identities determine the Clebsch structure. All finite certificates admit independent verification using integer arithmetic.
item.dc:creator: Youwen Xu

item.title: Four runners that are barely lonely
item.description: arXiv:2610.40694v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For positive integers $v_1,\dots,v_n$ let $\mathrm{ML}(v_1,\dots,v_n)=\max_t\min_i\|v_it\|$, where $\|x\|$ is the distance to the nearest integer. Kravitz asked which values below $1/n$ occur. For $n=4$, Jain and Kravitz showed that the values below $1/4$ are $m/(4m+2)$, $m\ge2$, up to finitely many undetermined exceptions. We settle the four-runner case completely. A primitive quadruple has $\mathrm{ML}<1/4$ if and only if it is, up to order, $\{1,2,3,4k\}$, or $\{x,y,x+y,x+2y\}$ with $\gcd(x,y)=1$ and $y\not\equiv x,2x\pmod 4$, or $\{1,3,4,14\}$. The values below $1/4$ are exactly $m/(4m+2)$ with $m\ge2$, $m\ne3$, so $3/14$ is the only exception, and Conjecture 4.1 of Fan and Sun holds. A density lemma bounds the length of a quadruple on neither critical subtorus by $512$, and an exact search over 800,816,099 quadruples completes the proof. The same method shows that the two-dimensional subtori of $(\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z})^4$ with loneliness below $2/5$ take exactly the three-runner values in that range, which between $1/3$ and $2/5$ are the fractions $p/q$ with $1\le 2q-5p\le 4$. Hence the accumulation points of the four-runner spectrum in $(0,2/5]$ are the three-runner values there, as Giri and Kravitz conjectured, and $9/25$ is not the loneliness of a two-dimensional subtorus. For every $n$, assuming the conjecture for $n-1$ and $n-2$ speeds, we prove $\mathrm{ML}(v)>1/n-(n(n-1))^{n-2}/(2|v|)$, which is sharp in $|v|$, and that every $n$-tuple with $\mathrm{ML}<1/n$ and $|v|\ge n(n(n-1))^{2n-4}$ lies on a two-dimensional subtorus of loneliness $1/n$. This answers a question of Cordella. For five speeds, a two-dimensional subtorus of $(\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z})^5$ with loneliness below $2/9$ is the product of a coordinate circle with the circle of $\{1,2,3,4\}$ or $\{1,3,4,7\}$. We also give infinitely many subtori whose maximizers lie off every circle with a repeated speed.
item.dc:creator: Hyunjun Yi, Karam Gill, Bryan Bu

item.title: Asymptotic stability of clique-saturating edges near Tur\'an thresholds
item.description: arXiv:2610.40696v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $f_{p+1}(n,m)$ denote the minimum number of $K_{p+1}$-saturating edges in an $n$-vertex $K_{p+1}$-free graph with $m$ edges. In this paper, we investigate the stability of this parameter near the Tur\'an thresholds, with particular emphasis on the role of the minimum degree. We introduce the refined parameter $f_{p+1,p}(n,m,\delta)$. It is defined for $K_{p+1}$-free graphs on $n$ vertices with $m$ edges, minimum degree $\delta$, and containing at least a copy of $K_p$. For every fixed integer $p\ge3$, we establish a stability result when the number of edges is $\mathrm{ex}(n,K_p)+o(n^2)$, showing that \[ f_{p+1,p} (n,m,\delta)=\left(\frac{(p-2)^2}{2(p-1)^3}+o(1)\right)n^2, \ \text{for }\ m=\mathrm{ex}(n,K_p)+o(n^2), \ \delta\geq \left(\frac{p-2}{p-1}+o(1)\right)n. \] We further obtain a stability theorem in the regime where the number of edges is quadratically smaller than $\operatorname{ex}(n,K_{p+1})$. More precisely, for $0 \leq c< \frac{1}{2p(3p-1)}$, \[ f_{p+1,p} (n,m,\delta)=\left(\frac{1}{2p}+o(1)\right)n^2, \ \text{for }\ m=\operatorname{ex}(n,K_{p+1})-(c+o(1))n^2, \ \delta\geq \left(\frac{p-1}{p}-2c+o(1)\right)n. \]
item.dc:creator: Xianglei Chen, Changxiang He

item.title: The Hibi--Li (2016) conjecture is fully resolved
item.description: arXiv:2610.40703v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hibi and Li conjectured that the order polytope $\mathcal{O}(P)$ of a finite poset $P$ has at most as many faces of each dimension as its chain polytope $\mathcal{C}(P)$, and that equality in some dimension $k$ with $1\leq k\leq|P|-1$ forces the two polytopes to be unimodularly equivalent. Fourier proved the inequality in a 2026 preprint. Let $X$ be the five-element poset in which an element lies above two incomparable elements and below two other incomparable elements. Building on Fourier's proof, we show that if an $n$-element poset contains $X$ as an induced subposet, then, for every $k$ with $2\leq k\leq n-1$, its chain polytope has at least $\binom{n-3}{k-2}$ more $k$-dimensional faces than its order polytope, and that for every $n\geq5$ some $n$-element poset containing $X$ attains all these bounds at once. Since Hibi and Li showed that $\mathcal{O}(P)$ and $\mathcal{C}(P)$ are unimodularly equivalent exactly when $P$ does not contain $X$, this proves the equality statement for these $k$. For $k=1$ the equality statement is false: $\mathcal{O}(X)$ and $\mathcal{C}(X)$ have equally many edges (Hibi, Li, Sahara and Shikama) but are not unimodularly equivalent. With Fourier's inequality, these results settle the conjecture. Every result is formally verified in Lean 4, with only published results and two results of Fourier's preprint as axioms.
item.dc:creator: Dave Goel

item.title: Anti-concentration and Graham's rearrangement problem in finite abelian groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.40712v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $S$ be a subset of $n$ elements of a group $G$. An ordering $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ of its elements is valid if the partial sums $x_1,x_1+x_2,\ldots,x_1+\cdots+x_n$ are pairwise distinct. This notion has a long history in combinatorial group theory, dated back to Gordon's works in early 1960. Alspach-Liversidge conjecture asserts that any subset of the nonzero elements of a finite abelian group $G$ has a valid ordering. This generalizes Graham's conjecture, which considers the case when the group $G$ is $\mathbb{F}_p$, the cyclic group of prime order. Graham's conjecture has been solved recently, as a combination of results by Kravitz, Bedert and Kravitz, M\"uyesser and Pokrovskiy, Bedert, Buci\'c, Kravitz, Montgomery, and M\"uyesser, and Pham and Sauermann. Beside this, the only other case where Alspach-Liversidge conjecture has been confirmed is $G=\mathbb{F}_2^k$, thanks to a recent result by Bedert, Buci\'c, Kravitz, Montgomery, and M\"uyesser. We prove the Alspach-Liversidge conjecture in its full generality. Our proof combines ideas from many previous papers. In particular, we will use the probabilistic approach and the absorption method. Our new main technical ingredient is a Fourier-moment estimate, which is of independent interest. In particular, we can use it to show that the distribution of certain kinds of random sums in an abelian group has an almost uniform distribution.
item.dc:creator: Hoi H. Nguyen, Tuan Tran, Van H. Vu

item.title: The Cranston--Li--Su--Wang--Xu (2026) conjecture is true
item.description: arXiv:2610.40863v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $A$ be a finite abelian group. A nowhere-zero $A$-flow of a graph gives every edge a direction and a non-zero value in $A$, so that at every vertex the sum of the values on the entering edges equals the sum on the leaving edges. Such a flow can be changed along a cycle: going around the cycle, add a fixed non-zero element of $A$ to the value of every edge that points forward and subtract it from the value of every edge that points backward. The Cranston--Li--Su--Wang--Xu (2026) conjecture states that if $A$ has at least four elements, then in every graph in which all degrees are even, any two nowhere-zero $A$-flows are joined by a chain of such changes through nowhere-zero $A$-flows. It also states that, for every integer $k\ge 4$, the same holds for integer flows whose values are between $1$ and $k-1$ in absolute value, where each change adds a non-zero integer. We prove this conjecture. The core of the proof is an induction on the number of edges: if a flow enters a vertex $v$ along an edge $uv$ and leaves $v$ along an edge $vw$ with the same value, the two edges can be replaced by one edge $uw$, and the induction hypothesis applies to the smaller graph. So the main task is to change every flow into a flow with such a pair of edges. For nowhere-zero $A$-flows with $|A|\ge 4$, replacing vertices of degree more than $4$ by triangles reduces the problem to graphs with all degrees at most $4$. For integer flows, a counting argument joins any two nowhere-zero flows with values in the cyclic group $\mathbb{Z}_k$, $k\ge 4$, by changes that add $1$, $-1$, $2$ or $-2$; every such chain gives a chain of integer flows with values between $1$ and $k-1$ in absolute value, and every integer flow of this chain reduces modulo $k$ to a flow of the given chain. All results of this paper are also proved in the Lean 4 proof assistant, from Lean's standard axioms alone.
item.dc:creator: Dave Goel

item.title: Foatic Homomesy
item.description: arXiv:2610.40882v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Using a unified method of identifying a telescoping function for each statistic-action pair, we prove conjectures of La Croix and Roby, and of Sheridan-Rossi that various permutation statistics, such as the number of fixed points, are homomesic under Foatic actions: compositions of the Foata bijection and dihedral symmetries of one-line notation. Underlying these results is a family of bijective identities relating permutation statistics across the Foata bijection; one of them --- an unexpected invariance of the number of right-to-left minima under reverse-complement, proved by an explicit bijection --- may be of independent interest. The telescoping functions also turn out to be shared among some Foatic actions, implying that mixing certain actions still yields a constant average on closed walks.
item.dc:creator: Peter Mao

item.title: An explicit bound on the extremal function for complete graph minors
item.description: arXiv:2610.41060v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Kostochka and Thomason independently proved that every graph with density at least $\beta\,t\sqrt{\log t}$ has a $K_t$ minor, for some constant $\beta$. Thomason later proved that the least such density is $(0.319\ldots+o(1))\,t\sqrt{\log t}$. However, the $o(1)$ term in this formula is not explicit, so the formula gives no bound for any specific value of $t$. The goal of this paper is a bound of the form $\beta\,t\sqrt{\log t}$ that holds for every $t$, with $\beta$ small. We prove that, for every integer $t\geqslant2$, every graph with density at least $4.5\,t\sqrt{\log t}$ has a $K_t$ minor.
item.dc:creator: David R. Wood

item.title: Unavoidable flats in matroids excluding a uniform minor
item.description: arXiv:2610.41096v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We extend a theorem of Geelen, Kroeker, and Nelson on unavoidable flats in $\operatorname{GF}(q)$-representable matroids. For all integers $1\le a\le b$ and $n\ge1$, we prove that every simple matroid of sufficiently large rank with no $U_{a,b}$-minor has a rank-$n$ flat whose restriction is free or isomorphic to a projective or affine geometry over a finite field.
item.dc:creator: Wayne Ge

item.title: Variance Bounds and Strict Log-Concavity for Forest Coronas
item.description: arXiv:2610.41102v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the size of a random independent set in every nonempty forest has variance strictly smaller than its mean at common activity $0<t\le1$. A rooted quadratic reserve gives quantitative forms of this inequality. Mean matching transfers the bounds to fixed-weight canonical completion laws, and exact binomial moments prove strict log-concavity for every forest corona and every well-covered forest. The stronger factorial normalization $((m-j)!i_j)_{j=0}^m$ is strictly log-concave; we give explicit coefficient margins, terminal sharpness, one-less smoothing, and the exact universal three-index binomial ULC prefix. An exact attachment argument doubles the rooted reserve for every nontrivial unweighted tree. For a single marked root, a square reserve holds through $\Theta=\tfrac12e^{3-2W(1/e)}$ and for every positive mark at roots of degree at most four. A stronger reserve holds through mark $15/14$. These estimates yield marked clique, adjacent-pair, and repulsive two-piece variance bounds with fixed-weight canonical transfer. Finally, arbitrary positive site activities in $[3t/4,t]$ satisfy a uniform rooted reserve on every forest. This proves strict log-concavity for weighted forest coronas with compatible base marks. An explicit weighted-star obstruction shows why an unrestricted heterogeneous extension is impossible. Complete proofs are included, together with the required classical graph characterization and variance comparison.
item.dc:creator: Vadim E. Levit

item.title: Deck Reconstruction for Restricted Word Classes
item.description: arXiv:2610.41110v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a binary word $x\in \{0,1\}^+$, the $k$-deck of $x$ is the multiset of all length-$k$ subsequences counted with multiplicity. The deck reconstruction problem asks for the minimum $k$ such that every word of a fixed length is uniquely determined by its $k$-deck. In this paper, we study deck reconstruction for several restricted classes of binary words, including words with exactly $s$ ones, words with at most $\ell$ runs of ones, and words where the indices of ones are given by a monotone polynomial of degree $d$. We prove that for these classes of words, their reconstruction thresholds are bounded by a function of the structural complexity of the class. We also study weak deck reconstruction, in which subwords may contain "wildcard" symbols that map to either 0 or 1. By generalizing a "template lemma" of Dud\'ik and Schulman, we improve the upper bound in an open question about weak reconstruction from Dud\'ik and Schulman. Finally, for the class of periodic words with period $d$, we prove that its in-class reconstruction threshold is equal to the general reconstruction threshold for words of length $d$, and give a general template construction producing further classes with the same threshold-preservation phenomenon.
item.dc:creator: Krishna Angal, Ruben Ascoli, Simon X. He, Xiaoyu He, Logan Post, Arker Oke Soe, Olga Zhukova

item.title: Circular regular dessins with underlying graphs ${\bf K}_{2^e,2^f}^{(2^d)}$: the metacyclic case
item.description: arXiv:2610.41123v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A dessin is a 2-cell embedding of a connected bipartite graph into an orientable closed surface. It is regular if the colour- and orientation-preserving automorphism group acts regularly on edges, and circular if every face boundary is a simple cycle. We classify and enumerate circular regular dessins of the complete bipartite multigraph ${\bf K}_{2^e,2^f}^{(2^d)}$ ($e\ge f\ge 2$, $d\ge 1$) whose automorphism group is {\it metacyclic}. This extends the work of Fan (circular, metacyclic) and Cai--Hu (regular, metacyclic) from simple graphs ${\bf K}_{2^e,2^f}$ to multigraphs ${\bf K}_{2^e,2^f}^{(2^d)}$. Such dessins correspond to non-exact bicyclic factorisations $G=\l a\r\l b\r\cong\ZZ_{2^{e+d}}\ZZ_{2^{f+d}}$, where $\l a\r\cap\l b\r\cong\ZZ_{2^d}$ and $\l ba\r\cap \l a\r=\l ba\r\cap \l b\r=1$. In general, a group admitting such a factorisation need not be metacyclic; in this paper we impose the additional condition that $G$ is a metacyclic 2-group. Under this assumption, we obtain explicit enumeration formulas for the number of such dessins up to isomorphism. Together with the known classifications for simple graphs (the case $d=0$), this completes the enumeration of the metacyclic case for 2-power complete bipartite multigraphs.
item.dc:creator: Yuntian Wu, Wenwen Fan

item.title: Changing parameters in Hall-Littlewood functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.41155v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the transition coefficients $b_{\lambda,\mu}(q,t)$ of the Hall--Littlewood $P$-functions $P_\lambda(t)$ expanded in the basis $P_\mu(q)$. We find a tableaux formula when $\lambda$ is a hook shape which generalizes term-by-term Lascoux-Schutzenberger's charge formula as well as Macdonald's monomial expansion formula for Hall-Littlewood functions. We conjecture that $b_{\lambda,\mu}(t+1,t)\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}[t]$ and prove it when $\lambda$ is a hook shape, when $\lambda$ has two-columns and some more simple cases. We prove that $b_{\lambda,\mu}(t+n,n)\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}[t]$ for every $n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}$, extending work of Alexandersson, and we record a stability property and some reduction principles.
item.dc:creator: Aritra Bhattacharya, Ziyi Dai, Qilin Hou, Edward Tong

item.title: Rainbow Hamiltonian paths in graph collections under edge-size conditions
item.description: arXiv:2610.41203v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\mathbf{G}=\{G_1,\dots,G_{n-1}\}$ be a collection of not necessarily distinct graphs of order $n$ on the same vertex set $V$. A path $P$ with $V(P)\subseteq V$ is called \emph{rainbow} in $\mathbf{G}$, if there exists an injection $\phi\colon E(P)\to [n-1]$ such that $e\in E(G_{\phi(e)})$ for each $e\in E(P)$. In this paper, we show that if $n\ge3$, $e(G_i)> \binom{n-2}{2}+2$ for each $i\in[n-1]$ and $G_j$ is connected for some $j\in[n-1]$, then there exists a rainbow Hamiltonian path in $\mathbf{G}$ unless $n=6$ with $G_1=G_2=\dots=G_{5}\cong K_2\vee 4K_1$, or $n=8$ with $G_1=G_2=\dots=G_{7}\cong K_3\vee 5K_1$. This corrects Theorem 6 in [Graphs Combin., \textbf{41}(6)(2025), 119] and relaxes its hypothesis from requiring all $G_i$ to be connected to only requiring that at least one $G_i$ is connected, where $i\in[n-1]$. Moreover, we show that if $n\ge2$ and $e(G_i)\ge \binom{n-1}{2}$ for each $i\in[n-1]$, then $\mathbf{G}$ contains a rainbow Hamiltonian path unless $G_1=G_2=\dots=G_{n-1}\cong K_{n-1}\cup K_1$, or $n=4$ with $G_1=G_2=G_3\cong K_{1,3}$. As a consequence, Theorem 2 of [Discrete Math., \textbf{347}(2024), 114128] follows immediately.
item.dc:creator: Xiaoxue Zhang, Lihua You

item.title: A note on decompositions into 3-chromatic graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.41266v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Delcourt and Postle recently introduced the `discharging in the dual' proof technique, leading to a breakthrough proof of Nash-Williams' conjecture on triangle decompositions. Independently, and almost simultaneously, the first and second authors built on the `condensation' method of Bryant, Dukes, Horsley, Maenhaut and Montgomery to determine the decomposition threshold of all odd cycles of length at least $73$. In this note, we explain how the `discharging in the dual' and `condensation' methods can be combined to determine the decomposition threshold of cycles of any odd length, as well as the approximate decomposition threshold of a range of other $3$-chromatic graphs.
item.dc:creator: Bertille Granet, Daniel Horsley, Jeffrey N. Santrio

item.title: On the Tur\'an number for the Cartesian product of an odd cycle and a tree
item.description: arXiv:2610.41286v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $T$ be a fixed tree on at least two vertices. We determine the Tur\'an number and all extremal graphs for the Cartesian product of an odd cycle $C_{2m+1}$ and $T$, for every fixed integer $m\ge1$ and all sufficiently large $n$, in terms of its decomposition family. Every extremal graph is the join of an independent set and an extremal graph for that family. The proof combines the Erd\H{o}s--S\'os theorem with weak stability and progressive induction.
item.dc:creator: Ya-Hong Chen, Yong Lu, Quan Sun, Qi Wu, Long-Tu Yuan

item.title: Pebbling Numbers and Generator Reinforcement of Cayley Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.41306v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study inverse-closed generator additions of minimum size that make the optimal pebbling number of a finite Cayley graph at most three while preserving its specified regular action. A weighted vertex-cover formulation on inverse orbits yields an $O(|\Gamma|^2)$ algorithm for abelian groups in the explicit multiplication-table model. We derive formulas for central involutions and cubelike graphs, with an inverse-closure correction determined by square roots in the uncovered set. The exact thresholds are $2^{d-1}-d$ for hypercubes ($d\ge1$), and $3$ for standard Keller graphs when $d=2$ and $2^{d-1}$ when $d\ge3$. Every admissible augmentation of either family has ordinary pebbling number equal to its order.
item.dc:creator: Yuan Yang, Bocheng Li, Qingzhong Ji

item.title: Clique-factors in randomly perturbed hypergraphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.41340v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we establish the following result for clique-factors in randomly perturbed hypergraphs when the cliques are large enough. For integers $k \geq 3$ and $t\geq t_0(k)$, we show that for every $\alpha> 0$, there exists $C>0$ such that for sufficiently large $n\in(t+1)\mathbb{N}$, the union of a $k$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices with minimum codegree at least $\alpha n$ and a binomial random $k$-uniform hypergraph $H^{(k)}(n,p)$ with $p\geq Cn^{-{t/\binom{t+1}{k}}}$ on the same vertex set contains a $K_{t+1}^{(k)}$-factor asymptotically almost surely. The bound on $p$ is asymptotically best possible and extends the graph case, resolved by Balogh, Treglown and Wagner. In particular, we have $t_0(3)=3$, which implies that our result applies to every $t\ge 3$ for $3$-uniform hypergraphs. Together with the previously established result for perfect matchings, this covers all possible clique sizes for $3$-uniform hypergraphs.
item.dc:creator: Yulin Chang, Jie Han, Patrick Morris, Lin Sun

item.title: Separating hash families with large universe II
item.description: arXiv:2610.41353v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For fixed integers $t,k\ge 2$, put $N=(t-1)(k-1)+1$. We prove that the maximum universe size of a $t$-perfect hash family of length $N$ over an alphabet of size $q$ satisfies $ p_t(N,q)\ge q^{k-o(1)}$. Together with monotonicity in the length, this gives a positive answer to a question of Blackburn, Etzion, Stinson and Zaverucha for every choice of feasible parameters. Our proof combines the Nash--Williams--Tutte theorem, a graph-theoretic elimination argument, and a solution-free-set theorem established in our previous work.
item.dc:creator: Xin Wei, Gennian Ge

item.title: Two-coloring the points of a projective plane
item.description: arXiv:2610.41357v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let us color the points of a projective plane of odd order $n$ with two colors, say red and blue. Erd\H{o}s asked the question of determining the maximum number of balanced lines (that have the same number of red and blue points). The answer is $n^2$, and in the corresponding trivial coloring the unbalanced lines go through a point. In this paper, we consider the Galois plane $\mathrm{PG}(2,q)$ and determine the number of unbalanced lines for a non-trivial coloring. The problem can also be generalized to $(r,b)$-colored lines (see Definition 1.1) and in many cases we extend the results to the generalized problem. Our strongest result for Galois planes of prime order $p$ describes all 2-colorings with at most $\max\{3p+1,4p-22\}$ not $(r,b)$-colored lines (see Theorem 5.13). Finally, in case of the generalized problem, we allow even more not $(r,b)$-colored lines if $r$ is small and the order is prime (for more details, see Theorem 5.18).
item.dc:creator: Aart Blokhuis, \'Ad\'am Mark\'o, Tam\'as Sz\H{o}nyi, Zsuzsa Weiner

item.title: $K_r$-Packings in Graphs with $t_{r-1}(n)+k$ Edges
item.description: arXiv:2610.41371v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fix an integer $r\ge 3$. Let $K_r$ denote the complete graph on $r$ vertices and $t_{r-1}(n)$ the Tur\'an number for $K_r$. For each integer $k$ satisfying $0\le k \le \binom{n}{2}-t_{r-1}(n)$, $\rev{\phi_r(n,k)}$ denotes the minimum, over all $n$-vertex graphs with $t_{r-1}(n)+k$ edges, of the maximum size of a $K_r$-packing \rev{(a family of edge-disjoint copies of $K_r$)} in the graph. The problem of characterizing the behavior of $\phi_r(n,k)$ has a long history and dates back to Erd\H{o}s for the case $r=3$. \rev{Gy\H{o}ri} proved that $\phi_r(n,k)=(1-o(1))k$ whenever $k=o(n^2)$. We characterize the range of $k$ for which $\phi_r(n,k)=(1-o(1))k$, showing that this equality holds if and only if $k=o(n^2)$. Moreover, we obtain an \rev{asymptotic} upper bound (which falls below $1$) for $\phi_r(n,k)/k$ whenever $k/n^2$ converges to a constant $\delta$ satisfying $0 < \delta \le \frac{1}{2(r-1)}$.
item.dc:creator: Hanzhi Bai, Fuhong Ma, Jin Yan

item.title: New results on openly disjoint cycles in regular digraphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.41372v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given a digraph \(D\), let \(c(D)\) be the largest size of a collection of openly disjoint directed cycles through a common vertex, and let \(c_r\) be the minimum of \(c(D)\) over all \(r\)-regular digraphs \(D\). In 2005, Seymour asked whether every \(r\)-regular digraph satisfies \(c(D)=r\). Mader answered Seymour's problem negatively for every \(r\ge 8\), but conjectured that nevertheless \(\lim_{r\to\infty}c_r=\infty\). Recently, Steiner confirmed this conjecture by proving \[ \left\lceil \frac{3r}{22}\right\rceil \le c_r \le 7\left\lceil \frac{r}{8}\right\rceil. \] In this paper, we first answer Seymour's problem negatively for $r\in \{6,7\}$, and then improve Steiner's bound to \[ \left\lceil \frac{r}{6}\right\rceil \le c_r \le 5\left\lceil \frac{r}{6}\right\rceil.\]
item.dc:creator: Bin Chen, Wenshen Wu, Meishaung Chen

item.title: The lattice of antichains of intervals: Dyck paths, level sets, and sweep dimension
item.description: arXiv:2610.41385v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Clarke-Cormack-Burkowski lattice $\mathcal{E}_n$ is the lattice of antichains of intervals of the chain $\{0,1,\dots,n-1\}$, the algebraic structure underlying minimal-interval semantics, a query semantics used in information retrieval. We give an explicit, elementary anti-isomorphism between $\mathcal{E}_n$ minus its top element and the Stanley lattice of Dyck words of semilength $n+1$ (an anti-isomorphism whose existence is implicit in work of Ferrari and Munarini), under which the rank of an antichain is $\binom{n+1}{2}$ minus the area of the associated Dyck word. Hence the rank generating function of $\mathcal{E}_n\setminus\{\top\}$ is the reverse of the Carlitz-Riordan $q$-Catalan polynomial. Using a local limit theorem for the area of random-walk excursions, we confirm unconditionally an asymptotic formula of Tak\'acs: the size $\lambda_n$ of the largest level set of $\mathcal{E}_n$ satisfies $\lambda_n\sim\kappa\,4^{n+1}/(n+1)^3$, where $\kappa\approx1.0807$. Finally, for the antichains of intervals of an arbitrary finite poset $P$ we study the sweep dimension, the minimum number of linear orders needed to separate every interval from every element outside it. It equals the Dushnik-Miller dimension of the lattice of convex subsets of $P$, it is the least $k$ for which $P$ maps into $\mathbb{R}^k$ so that every interval is the preimage of an upper orthant, and it lies between $\max(2,w)$ and $2w$, where $w$ is the width of $P$, both bounds being tight. Antichains of intervals embed, preserving joins, into $k$-dimensional staircase regions.
item.dc:creator: Paolo Boldi, Sebastiano Vigna

item.title: Sink polynomials of line graphs and weighted matching polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2610.41502v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Chromatic quasisymmetric functions and unicellular LLT polynomials give symmetric-function interpretations of graph orientations counted by sinks. For natural unit interval graphs, we prove that the acyclic sink polynomial is real-rooted for every nonnegative ascent weight. Equivalently, the elementary coefficients of the chromatic quasisymmetric function, grouped by partition length, form a real-rooted polynomial. The Carlsson--Mellit relation expresses this polynomial as a plethystic specialization of the corresponding LLT polynomial, and the Hessenberg correspondence gives an interpretation in cohomology. More generally, the acyclic sink polynomial is real-rooted for chordal claw-free graphs, and the all-orientations sink polynomial is real-rooted for every claw-free graph. We also study a real-rooted polynomial counting joint minima in local edge orders. It agrees with the acyclic sink polynomial of the line graph exactly for forests. An exact formula for unicyclic roots gives a line-graph counterexample to acyclic sink real-rootedness.
item.dc:creator: Per Alexandersson, Leonardo Saud Maia Leite

item.title: Equivariant Ehrhart series for rational simplices and rational cross-polytopes
item.description: arXiv:2610.41529v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Equivariant Ehrhart theory was introduced by Stapledon (2011) and has since been extensively studied. A central question is whether the numerator in a certain rational function expression for the equivariant Ehrhart series is both a polynomial and effective. In this paper, we propose a modification of the denominator in the rational function expression for the equivariant Ehrhart series of rational polytopes. For rational simplices and rational cross-polytopes whose vertices have coordinates that are reciprocals of integers, we show that the resulting numerator is a polynomial and is effective. As an application of our results, we compute the equivariant series of the characteristic quasi-polynomials of root systems.
item.dc:creator: Ryo Uchiumi

item.title: On $t$-designs supported by self-orthogonal codes
item.description: arXiv:2610.41545v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study self-orthogonal $t$-$(v,k,\lambda)$ designs satisfying the condition that the codes generated by the designs are self-orthogonal codes whose codewords of minimum weight $k$ correspond to the blocks. A classification of such designs is given under the conditions that $t\geq \lfloor k/4\rfloor+1\geq2$ and $t \le 11$. This yields a classification of self-orthogonal codes of minimum weight $k$ whose codewords of minimum weight form a $t$-design under the same conditions.
item.dc:creator: Masaaki Harada

item.title: Haiman's conjecture for n <= 10: Kazhdan-Lusztig positivity of monomial immanants
item.description: arXiv:2610.41555v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Haiman conjectured that for every partition $\lambda\vdash n$ and every $w\in S_n$ the polynomial $c_{\lambda,w}(q)$, a monomial character of the Hecke algebra evaluated at the Kazhdan-Lusztig basis, has non-negative integer coefficients and is symmetric and unimodal, and he verified this by computer for $n\le7$. We verify it for every $n\le10$. A stability lemma reduces the statement to $n=10$, which we settle by an exact computation that stores only the 1,252,173,030 pairs $(x,w)$ in $S_{10}$ with $x$ maximal in its double coset for the descent sets of $w$, and takes the traces of the standard basis from the class polynomials of Geck and Pfeiffer. Every stored Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomial agrees with du Cloux's Coxeter3, and the coefficients pass several independent checks, including a comparison at all 16,796 codominant $w$ with chromatic quasisymmetric functions computed from colourings. Consequently, for $n\le10$ every monomial immanant is a non-negative integer combination of Kazhdan-Lusztig immanants, Stembridge's monomial immanant conjecture holds, and a class-function immanant is non-negative on totally non-negative matrices if and only if it is non-negative at the block matrices $J_\mu$. We use this to describe the order of normalised irreducible-character immanants on totally non-negative matrices for $n\le10$, and to prove Pate's inequalities there. On the full span of permutation monomials we give a Newton-polytope criterion for the coefficient of $\mathrm{Imm}_w$ to be non-negative throughout the totally non-negative cone, show that for $n=4,5$ this happens exactly when $X_w$ is smooth, and check by exact computation for $n\le10$ the proof of this for all $n$ given in a companion paper.
item.dc:creator: Keith McNulty

item.title: Perfect state transfer on unicyclic graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.41572v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We characterize adjacency perfect state transfer in connected unicyclic graphs: the transfer vertices are opposite degree-two vertices of a four-cycle, and the two attached trees satisfy a characteristic-polynomial condition. Except for the four-cycle, the transfer pair is unique and the minimum transfer time is $\pi/\sqrt2$. Outside the four-cycle, we obtain sharp lower bounds of $46$ on the order and $10$ on the maximum degree, and classify all examples of maximum degree at most $20$. A finite inverse construction enumerates all realizations of a prescribed eigenvalue support at the transfer vertices. For supports of size at least seven, we establish the sharp maximum-degree lower bound of $21$. Every seven-element support $\{0,\pm\sqrt2,\pm u\sqrt2,\pm v\sqrt2\}$, with odd integers $3\leq u<v$, is realizable, and every such realization has attachment depth at most four. Explicit branching rules give a minimum-order recurrence. Among all connected unicyclic graphs admitting perfect state transfer with seven-element eigenvalue support, the minimum order is $218$, attained uniquely up to isomorphism.
item.dc:creator: Xingkun Song

item.title: A Fan-Type Theorem for Hamiltonian Berge Cycles in 3-Uniform Hypergraphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.41577v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $H$ be a simple $3$-uniform hypergraph on $n\ge7$ vertices, and put $\tau_n=\binom{\lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor}{2}$. We prove that $H$ has a Hamiltonian Berge cycle if its $2$-shadow is $2$-connected, every pair at Berge distance two has an endpoint of hypergraph degree at least $\tau_n+1$, and every pair of codegree one has both endpoints above $\tau_n$. The distance-two threshold is sharp, and the order range cannot be extended to $n=4,5,6$. The proof separates two structural arguments. A low-degree endpoint of an extremal longest Berge path forces Hamiltonicity, independently of the order and the degree threshold. For high-degree endpoints, injective charging and its equality cases force pairs of codegree one that permit further rotations. The cases $n=7,8$ are settled by exhaustive verification, with a completeness proof and a second implementation using direct vertex--hyperedge cycle search. Keywords: Hamiltonian Berge cycle; Fan-type condition; 3-uniform hypergraph; longest-path rotation; exhaustive verification.
item.dc:creator: Ailian Chen, Yanqiang Liu

item.title: On sparse universally rigid graphs in $\mathbb{R}$
item.description: arXiv:2610.41581v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A graph is said to be 1-universally rigid if, for any generic realization of its vertices on the real line, the realization cannot be deformed out of the line in any higher-dimensional Euclidean space while preserving all edge lengths. In this paper, we investigate the sparsity of 1-universally rigid graphs in different manners. First, we show that an Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi random graph $G(n,p)$ is 1-universally rigid with high probability whenever $p \geq C\log n \cdot \log\log n/n$ for some sufficiently large constant $C>0$. These techniques also imply the existence of 1-universally rigid graphs of arbitrarily large girth, which resolves a problem suggested by Dantas e Moura, Jord\'an, and Silverman in a non-constructive manner. We also study how sparse a 1-universally rigid graph can be, proving that there exists an absolute constant $\varepsilon>0$ such that every sufficiently large 1-universally rigid graph on $n$ vertices has at least $(3/2+\varepsilon)n$ edges. This breaks the natural $3/2$ barrier arising from degree-2 extensions and makes progress towards a question of Jord\'an and Nguyen.
item.dc:creator: Ole Gabsdil, Ezra Hirschi, Julien Portier

item.title: Numerical Kawamata--Viehweg vanishing for rank-three matroids
item.description: arXiv:2610.41631v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the numerical Kawamata--Viehweg conjecture for every matroid of rank three: the Euler characteristic of the inverse of an integral big and nef line bundle class is nonnegative. The proof reduces the conjecture to an inequality for a stone game.
item.dc:creator: Ronnie Cheng

item.title: Proper conflict-free degree-choosability of graphs with maximum average degree less than $8/3$
item.description: arXiv:2610.41668v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A proper coloring $\varphi$ of a graph $G$ is called proper conflict-free if, for every non-isolated vertex $v$, some color appears exactly once in its open neighborhood $N_G(v)$. For a nonnegative integer $k$, a graph $G$ is proper conflict-free $(\mathrm{degree}+k)$-choosable if, for every list assignment $L$ satisfying $|L(v)|\ge d_G(v)+k$ for each $v\in V(G)$, there exists a proper conflict-free coloring $\varphi$ of $G$ with $\varphi(v)\in L(v)$ for each $v\in V(G)$. We prove that every connected graph other than the $5$-cycle $C_5$ with maximum average degree less than $8/3$ is proper conflict-free $(\mathrm{degree}+2)$-choosable. This improves the maximum average degree bound $18/7$ of Kashima, \v{S}krekovski and Xu, and removes the assumption $g(G)\ge7$ from the $8/3$ theorem of Qi, Song and Cao. As an immediate consequence, our theorem also yields that every planar graph of girth at least $8$ is proper conflict-free $(\mathrm{degree}+2)$-choosable.
item.dc:creator: Huijuan Xu

item.title: CRCs in four-dimensional lattice graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.41716v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We obtain series of new completely regular codes in Cayley graphs of the groups $Z_q^n$ with the Lee metric. Combined with binary linear programming methods, the constructions lead to enumeration of all completely regular codes in such graphs for the groups $Z_q^4$, $q\leq 7$ up to parameter matrices.
item.dc:creator: Ivan Mogilnykh

item.title: Maximum edge overlap between independent random regular graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.41735v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Optimising the vertex correspondence can substantially increase the number of edges shared by two independent realisations of the same random graph. We quantify this phenomenon for uniformly random $d$-regular graphs and derive corresponding results for their edge-based graph edit distance. For every fixed $d\geq 3$, we show that the maximum overlap is $n+\Theta_{\mathbb P}(n/\log n)$, where the leading term $n$ arises from Hamiltonicity, while the surplus captures the optimal order of the excess beyond it. We establish explicit upper and lower bounds on the surplus. The upper bound is obtained by counting common cores of minimum degree at least two, while the lower bound is established using spanning factors consisting of cycles of the same logarithmic length. For the special case $d=2$, we show that the maximum overlap is $n-(1+o_{\mathbb P}(1))\log n$. The additional overlap achievable is also studied by rotating aligned Hamilton cycles, using a contiguity argument. As a by-product, we determine the asymptotic maximum overlap between unions of independent random perfect matchings under cyclic shifts.
item.dc:creator: Andrea D'Ascenzo, Riccardo Michielan

item.title: Bounds on the maximum denominator of fractional chromatic numbers
item.description: arXiv:2610.41771v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a positive rational number $x=p/q$, where $p$ and $q$ are coprime positive integers, let $\operatorname{den}(x)=q$. For a positive integer $n$, let $\operatorname{sd}(n)=\max\{\operatorname{den}(\chi_f(G)): |V(G)|=n\}$. Let $D(n)=2^{-n}(n+1)^{(n+1)/2}$. It was proved by Alon, Tuza and Voigt that $\operatorname{sd}(n)\le D(n)$. In this paper, we prove that $\operatorname{sd}(n)\le D(n)n^{-\frac12\log_2 n+\frac14\log_2\log_2 n+O(1)}$ for all sufficiently large $n$. For the lower bound on $\operatorname{sd}(n)$, it was recently proved by Bonamy, Hylasov\'a, Kaiser and Sereni that $\limsup_{n\to\infty}\operatorname{sd}(n)^{1/n}\ge\sqrt{2}$. We prove that $\limsup_{n\to\infty}\operatorname{sd}(n)^{1/n}\ge 3^{1/3}>\sqrt{2}$.
item.dc:creator: Xinbo Xu, Xuding Zhu

item.title: Ore-degree conditions for hypergraph matchings
item.description: arXiv:2610.41787v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\sigma_k(H)$ be the minimum sum of the vertex degrees over all non-edges of an $n$-vertex $k$-uniform hypergraph $H$. For every $k\ge3$, $n\geq ks$ and sufficiently large $n$, we establish a sharp Ore-type degree condition that forces a matching of size $s$ in $H$. Specifically, we prove that if \[ \sigma_k(H)>\max\left\{ k\left(\binom{n-1}{k-1}-\binom{n-s}{k-1}\right), (k-c)\binom{ks-2}{k-1}\right\}, \] then $H$ has a matching of size $s$, where $c=n-ks+1$. In particular, this proves a conjecture of Balogh, Palmer and Raeisi for $k\geq 3$ and sufficiently large $n$.
item.dc:creator: Mingyang Guo, Tianhong Kan, Hongliang Lu, Feihong Yuan

item.title: The Alon-Tarsi number of 4-regular circulant graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.41820v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies the Alon-Tarsi number of connected $4$-regular circulant graphs $C_n(s,t)$, where $1\le s<t<n/2$. We prove that if $n=\ell p^r$, where $p$ is an odd prime, $r\ge 1$, and $t\equiv\pm s\pmod{\ell}$, then $\operatorname{AT}(C_n(s,t))=3$ if $\ell$ is even, or if $\ell\ge 3$ is odd and $p\nmid 2^\ell-2$. We also prove that $\operatorname{AT}(C_{6m}(2,3))=3$ for $m\ge 2$, and $\operatorname{AT}(C_n(1,3))=3$ for $n\ge 8$.
item.dc:creator: Xinbo Xu, Xuding Zhu

item.title: Revisiting the directed pathwidth of h-semicomplete digraphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.41840v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A digraph is $h$-semicomplete if every vertex has at most $h$ non-neighbors. In semicomplete digraphs, $k$-triples are obstructions to bounded directed pathwidth with many algorithmic applications: Fradkin and Seymour [JCTB 2013] showed that a large triple contains a subdivision of every small digraph, and triples were used for irrelevant vertex arguments in routing problems by Fomin and Pilipczuk [JCTB 2019] and Gomes, Lopes, and Sau [ICALP 2025]. Fradkin and Seymour also showed that there is a function $f(k)$ such that every semicomplete digraph of directed pathwidth at least $f(k)$ contains a $k$-triple, and their proof gives $f(k)$ triply exponential in $k$. For $h$-semicomplete digraphs, a result of Kitsunai et al. [ESA 2015] also yields a $k$-triple, but only existentially, and finding one in fixed-parameter time remained open. We improve the bound on $f(k)$ to a single exponential and extend the result to $h$-semicomplete digraphs: we show that every $h$-semicomplete digraph of directed pathwidth greater than $(h+1) \cdot k \cdot 2^{27k+9}$ contains a $k$-triple, which we find in polynomial time, and no bound subexponential in $k$ or sublinear in $h$ is possible. We also extend the approximation algorithm for directed pathwidth of Fomin and Pilipczuk to $h$-semicomplete digraphs, so its certificates of large directed pathwidth remain valid. Our proof is much shorter than the analysis of Kitsunai et al., and while their algorithm is exact, ours runs in polynomial time. As an application, we show that Arc-Disjoint Paths on $h$-semicomplete digraphs is fixed-parameter tractable parameterized by the number of paths and $h$, generalizing the semicomplete case. Finally, unlike in semicomplete digraphs, directed pathwidth does not bound directed cliquewidth: for every $k$, some acyclic $1$-semicomplete digraph, so of directed pathwidth zero, has directed cliquewidth at least $k$.
item.dc:creator: Guilherme C. M. Gomes, Raul Lopes, Matthias Mnich

item.title: Strong edge-colourings of truncations of cubic graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.41950v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a problem posed by Kardo\v{s} asking whether the truncation of every connected simple bridgeless cubic graph has strong chromatic index six. The truncation $T(G)$ is obtained by replacing each vertex of $G$ with a triangle and attaching its incident edges to distinct vertices of that triangle. An affirmative answer was previously established for prism bases by Han and Cui. We prove that $\sidx(T(G))=6$ whenever $G$ is a connected simple cubic graph that is bipartite or is both bridgeless and claw-free. Both proofs are constructive and use a common compatibility criterion for combining colourings of smaller pieces. The bipartite result also extends to non-det-extremal multigraphs.
item.dc:creator: Domenico Labbate, Federico Romaniello

item.title: The 3-Color 2-Chromatic Gallai-Ramsey Number for Complete Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.41971v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For $1\le i\le j\le k$, let $gr^3_2(K_i, K_j, K_k)$ be the least $n\in \mathbb{N}$ such that every rainbow triangle-free $3$-coloring of $K_n$ (using red, blue, and green) contains a red/blue $K_i$, a red/green $K_j$, or a blue/green $K_k$. In this paper, we completely evaluate $gr^3_2(K_i, K_j, K_k)$ for all values of $i$, $j$, and $k$ in which $r(K_i,K_j)$ is known.
item.dc:creator: Mark Budden, Elijah DeJonge

item.title: Hedetniemi's conjecture for Shannon OR-capacity: counterexamples and asymptotic separation
item.description: arXiv:2610.41977v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We disprove the analogue of Hedetniemi's conjecture for Shannon OR-capacity, which asserts that the capacity of a categorical product equals the smaller capacity of its factors. For every sufficiently large complete graph, we construct a second graph of larger capacity such that their categorical product has capacity strictly below that of the complete graph. Further constructions show that, for every real threshold above an explicit constant, both factor capacities can exceed that threshold while the product capacity lies below it. We also construct graph pairs, again with one complete factor, whose capacities tend to infinity while their product capacity is subpolynomial in the smaller factor capacity. Whether the product capacity must nevertheless tend to infinity whenever both factor capacities do remains open. The proofs use spectral interpolation, which also yields a single spectral point violating Hedetniemi's identity throughout the complete-factor family. Finally, we identify the categorical product as the distinguishability graph of a random-switching model for zero-error communication. In this model, our constructions show that switching can reduce the zero-error rate to a vanishing fraction of the smaller individual rate.
item.dc:creator: Julius A. Zeiss

item.title: Hilton-Zhao vertex-splitting conjecture for triangle-free graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.41984v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Every graph obtained from a regular Class $1$ graph by a vertex-splitting is overfull and hence is of Class $2$; the central question is whether the resulting graph is edge-chromatic critical. We consider a revised version of the Hilton-Zhao vertex-splitting conjecture for triangle-free base graphs, excluding the known cubic exception that arises from the Wagner graph. Let $G$ be a connected $n$-vertex triangle-free $\Delta$-regular Class $1$ graph, and let $G^{*}$ be obtained from $G$ by splitting one vertex into two adjacent vertices. We first show that any non-extreme vertex-splitting produces a $\Delta$-critical graph provided $\Delta>\frac{n-1}{3}$. Consequently, for non-extreme vertex-splittings, the revised version of the conjecture is valid across its entire conjectured degree range, and indeed even under a slightly weaker degree condition. We next turn to arbitrary vertex-splittings, extreme ones included. It is shown that $G^*$ is $\Delta$-critical provided $n \ge 10$ and $\Delta>\frac{2n-3}{5}$. In addition, for $n>24$, the non-strict condition $\Delta \ge \frac{2n-3}{5}$ is already sufficient. This extends the bipartite range $\Delta>\frac{2n}{5}$ to the boundary range that the bipartite argument does not cover. In particular, our arguments give a complete treatment of the case of triangle-free $6$-regular base graphs in the conjectured range. The proofs bring together structural properties of full-deficiency pairs, homomorphism theorems for dense triangle-free graphs, and Hamilton decompositions built via graph detachment.
item.dc:creator: Xuli Qi, Xin Tian, Gregory Gutin

item.title: Suspense and surprise in matroid bingo
item.description: arXiv:2610.41985v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present the game of Matroid Bingo and prove that it gets more suspenseful the longer the game goes on.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Baker

item.title: Ramsey numbers $R(K_{1,4},K_{m,n})$ for small $m$
item.description: arXiv:2610.41999v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine all currently unknown values of the generalized two-color Ramsey number $R(K_{1,4},K_{m,n})$ for $\min(m,n) \leq 8$. We also prove that the number $R(K_{1,4},K_{m,m})$ equals $26, 29, 31, 33$ for $m = 9, 10, 11, 12$ respectively.
item.dc:creator: Khaidar Abdullin, Dmitrii Taletskii

item.title: Tiling without a subspace complement: a sharp counterexample in dimension nine over the field with two elements
item.description: arXiv:2610.42005v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct an explicit 64-point subset of $\mathbb F_2^9$ which tiles by translation but has no linear-subspace tiling complement. Together with our earlier dimension-eight theorem and a product argument, this shows that every nonempty tile in $\mathbb F_2^d$ has a linear-subspace complement precisely when $d\le8$. The example is spectral, so it is not a counterexample to Fuglede's conjecture. Its construction uses six three-dimensional subspaces of $\mathbb F_2^6$, specified by a small table. We classify all its tiling complements and spectra: there are exactly 512 complements and 64 spectra, with one translation class of each. Every spectrum has normalized Wiener norm $15/8$. An appendix proves that Goyal's related construction is affinely inequivalent but has the same tiling complements and spectra. The construction and both classifications are proved from first principles. We also give elementary proofs of the positive assertion in dimensions at most seven and for all tile sizes other than sixteen in dimension eight. The remaining case uses our previously established theorem based on the classification of perfect binary codes of length fifteen.
item.dc:creator: Samuel J. Ferguson, Joshua Iosevich

item.title: Extremal character spectra of finite projective systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.42006v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\mathcal M$ be a finite spanning multiset of points in ${\rm PG}(k-1,q)$, and let ${\rm Char}_{\mathcal M}$ be its character function. For $1\le r\le k$, we study the maximum number of distinct values attained by ${\rm Char}_{\mathcal M}$ on the codimension-$r$ flats under a total-multiplicity budget. The spectrum is subject to two natural upper bounds, whose extremal cases lead respectively to $r$-maximum character spectrum ($r$-MCS) and $r$-full character spectrum ($r$-FCS) systems. We establish the existence of $r$-FCS systems in a broad parameter range, and solve the size-constrained extremal problem completely when $r=k-1$, including the minimum-cost multiplicity profiles. For $1\le r<k$, put $M_r=\qbinom{k}{r}$ and $B_r=\qbinom{k-1}{r}$. The minimum size $\nu_r(k,q)$ of an $r$-MCS system satisfies \[\left\lceil\frac{\binom{M_r}{2}}{B_r}\right\rceil\le \nu_r(k,q)\le \binom{M_r-1}{2}+\frac{q^k-q^{k-r}}{q-1}.\] The upper bound is at most $\binom{M_r}{2}$, strictly less when $r\le k-2$, and exact when $r=k-1$. Its proof applies positive additive labelings to the complement of one flat, whose trace is empty while all remaining traces are distinct. For $r=1$, we improve the known upper bounds on the minimum length of such systems. We also develop global moment identities and local flat-incidence bounds that impose strong structural constraints on large character spectra. Under the projective-system correspondence, complementary character spectra are the support-weight spectra of $r$-dimensional subcodes.
item.dc:creator: Shitao Li, Yang Li, Gaojun Luo

item.title: Modulo k-orientations of highly edge-connected signed graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.42019v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A modulo $k$-orientation of a signed graph is an orientation in which the outdegree and indegree are congruent modulo $k$ at every vertex. We show that, for every odd integer $k\ge3$, every essentially $k$-unbalanced $(6k-10)$-edge-connected signed graph admits a modulo $k$-orientation. This improves the edge-connectivity bound of Zhu [JCTB, 112 (2015)] from $6k-7$ to $6k-10$.
item.dc:creator: You Lu, Zhengke Miao, Zhenyu Tian, Cun-Quan Zhang

item.title: Berenstein-Zelevinsky polytopes for type $\mathrm{G}_{2}$
item.description: arXiv:2610.42038v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In 2001, Berenstein and Zelevinsky presented a polyhedral model for the problem of computing tensor-product multiplicities for semi\-simple Lie algebras. We provide explicit linear equations and inequalities for Berenstein--Zelevinsky (BZ) polytopes of type-$\mathrm{G}_{2}$ Lie algebras. We prove that the denominator of a type-$\mathrm{G}_{2}$ BZ~polytope divides $180$, and that this bound is sharp, while the quasi-period of the Ehrhart quasipolynomial of such a polytope is always a divisor of $6$. We also show that BZ~polytopes of type-$\mathrm{G}_{2}$ Lie algebras can fail to satisfy Ehrhart positivity, in contrast to a conjectured property of BZ~polytopes for all classical types.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Magnuson, Tyrrell McAllister

item.title: A Counterexample to the Alon-Krivelevich Conjecture and a New Lower Bound for Choosability of Bipartite Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.42094v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For an integer $k\ge 2$ and $r^2>2(2k-1)\ln (2k-1)$, we construct a bipartite graph $G$ whose two vertex classes are disjoint copies of the family of all $k$-subsets of a $(2k-1)$-element set, two vertices being adjacent when their sets intersect in at most $r$ elements. Assigning each vertex its corresponding subset as its color list, $G$ is not colorable, and thus its choice number $\ch(G)\ge k+1$. This implies that there are graphs with maximum degree $\Delta$ and $$\ch(G)\ge\Bigl(\frac1{32}-o(1)\Bigr)\frac{(\ln\Delta)^2}{(\ln\ln\Delta)^3}.$$ When $k\to\infty$, consequently $\ch(G)/\ln\Delta$ tends to infinity, which disproves the Alon--Krivelevich conjecture. In order to show the uncolorability, we use tools from probability (conditional product measure, nested coupling, and Doob martingale), which we write in an elementary language of weighted counting, and topology (Brouwer fixed-point theorem).
item.dc:creator: Junran Yu, Gexin Yu

item.title: On nowhere-zero ${3}$-flows in Cayley graphs on groups of order ${p^2n}$
item.description: arXiv:2610.42099v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider Tutte's $3$-flow conjecture in the class of Cayley graphs on groups $G$ of order $p^2n$, where $p$ is a prime and $n$ is square-free and coprime to $p$. The conjecture has been proved by J. Zhang and Z. Zhang in the case where $n$ is a prime (Discrete Mathematics, 2023); and by the authors in the case where $p=2$ (arXiv:2603.24175). In this paper, we prove the conjecture in the case where $p > 2$ and either a Sylow $p$-subgroup or a Hall $n$-subgroup of $G$ is a cyclic group.
item.dc:creator: Milad Ahanjideh, Istv\'an Kov\'acs

item.title: Weighted flip graphs from cyclic quantum mutations: pentagon inequalities and exponential separations
item.description: arXiv:2610.40661v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Positive cyclic quantum mutations at a third root of unity induce an explicit weight on polygon flip graphs. We study the resulting discrepancy between minimum flip count and minimum accumulated normalization loss. Every pentagon three-to-two replacement strictly decreases weight, and in connected types $A_1$, $A_2$, and $A_3$ every minimum-weight path is a flip geodesic. In type $A_4$, however, a six-flip path has smaller weight than the unique five-flip geodesic. A compatible positive projective gluing construction amplifies this example to an exponential success-probability separation in every connected type $A_n$, $n\ge4$. We also give a quantitative perturbation bound preserving the separation. The low-rank minimality statement has an exhaustive finite certificate; the pentagon inequality and the all-rank construction are analytic. In the associated sequential postselection model, differences of path weights determine success-probability ratios independently of the input state. The comparison holds for separately normalized exact mutation steps.
item.dc:creator: Xiaomin Tang

item.title: Tree-based Algorithms for Breakpoint Median and Near-Median Genomes
item.description: arXiv:2610.40667v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Median genomes serve as candidates for ancestral reconstruction and help study the diversity of parsimonious rearrangement solutions. However, the breakpoint median problem is NP-hard for unichromosomal genomes, and medians are non-unique, making their diversity important to study. In this paper, we develop tree-based algorithms for studying breakpoint medians of linear unichromosomal genomes represented as unsigned permutations. The algorithms construct rooted labeled trees whose leaves encode candidate median genomes satisfying local adjacency constraints derived from the inputs. We show that the resulting reduced search spaces contain all breakpoint medians while being much smaller than the full permutation space. We investigate these reduced spaces experimentally for three-genome instances. Our method finds exact medians and many near-optimal approximations, while early sampling of leaves often produces near-medians quickly. We also introduce constrained sampling procedures for targeting balanced near-medians, whose distances to the input genomes are more evenly distributed and hence are particularly relevant for ancestral reconstruction. The resulting framework provides a unified method for exact enumeration, efficient sampling, and targeted exploration of median and near-median genomes. In contrast to Traveling Salesman Problem-based approaches, which typically return a single solution and do not reveal the diversity or balance of the median set, our method can enumerate all medians, sample near-medians early, and target structurally distinct candidates under the breakpoint distance.
item.dc:creator: Poly H. da Silva, Arash Jamshidpey, David Sankoff

item.title: Truncated Grassmannians: polytopes, representations, and Cauchy formulas
item.description: arXiv:2610.40891v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The goal of this paper is to develop algebraic and combinatorial techniques for studying the geometric properties of truncated Grassmannians, a class of algebraic varieties obtained via certain projections of classical Grassmannians within their Pl\"ucker embeddings. We introduce a class of cyclic representations of maximal parabolic subalgebras of the general linear Lie algebra, which are proved to serve as duals of the homogeneous components of coordinate rings of truncated Grassmannians. We prove that the characters of these representations are computed via truncated Cauchy formulas and establish a connection with coordinate rings of complete collineations. We also construct monomial bases of these representations in terms of certain generalized chain polytopes and use the RSK correspondence to establish connections with Cauchy-type formulas and with Gelfand--Tsetlin patterns.
item.dc:creator: Evgeny Feigin, Igor Makhlin

item.title: Functorial Analysis of Group-Alphabet Cellular Automata
item.description: arXiv:2610.41013v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $G$ be a group and let $n\in\mathbb N$. We consider one-dimensional cellular automata of length $n$ over the alphabet $G$, with periodic boundary conditions and with local rules $\phi$ given by words. We construct a functor $F$ from $\mathbf{Grp}$, the category of groups (or any similar algebraic structure), to the category of pointed digraphs, and show its faithfulness. We introduce the image category $\mathcal C_{n,\phi}$ of state transition graphs of all such group-alphabet cellular automata, and show $F$ is an equivalence onto this category. Consequently we investigate the translation of categorical structures in $\mathbf{Grp}$ in terms of automata, and give examples of how standard methods of homological algebra may now be applied to automata. Additionally, a graph-theoretical construction of the product in $\mathcal C_{n,\phi}$ is given, together with a formula for cycle lengths and multiplicities in this product. When $G$ is abelian, further structural properties of state transition graphs follow, and we contrast these results with non-abelian counterexamples.
item.dc:creator: Fran\c{c}ois Huard, Nathan Dion Larivi\`ere

item.title: Rational curves of submaximal quantum index
item.description: arXiv:2610.41031v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: On a complex toric surface, oriented real rational curves tangent to the toric boundary at real points are distinguished by their value of quantum index. Using variants of usual Welschinger multiplicities, G. Mikhalkin defined enumerative invariants $W_{\tilde{\Delta}}^{\kappa}$ that are provided by a signed count of oriented real rational curves with given quantum index $\kappa$ and fixed tangency points on the boundary of the positive quadrant (the tangency orders being encoded by $\tilde{\Delta}$). We prove that, for most toric surfaces and tangency orders, the invariant $W_{\tilde{\Delta}}^{\kappa}$ is zero in the case of the highest nonmaximal value of $\kappa$. This is done by enumerating tropical curves with Block--G\"ottsche multiplicities. Additionally, we prove that, in many situations, the lower bound, given by the absolute value $|W_{\tilde{\Delta}}^{\kappa}|$ of $W_{\tilde{\Delta}}^{\kappa}$, for the number of oriented real rational curves is not sharp close to the tropical limit in the case of the highest nonmaximal value of $\kappa$.
item.dc:creator: Tangi Pasquer

item.title: Quantum Vehicle Routing Problem: a smart initialization strategy for ill-conditioned optimization landscapes
item.description: arXiv:2610.41120v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: With the expansion of complex transport infrastructure, new paths for linking different destinations have emerged, allowing the definition of multiple routes. The introduction of new roads may also lead to disruptions in traffic flow. This problem can be generalized into a special case of VRP, which aims to find the optimal route for a fleet of vehicles within a network of destinations. Finding solutions to this problem requires an exponential number of operations, hindering the ability of exact solvers to deal with large instances, which must therefore be tackled using heuristics, often leading to suboptimal results. Quantum-based algorithms may allow us to find exact solutions in polynomial time with high probability, offering a potential future alternative to classical solvers and in this work, we focus on the QAOA. Our novel contributions are a parameter-initialization strategy that improves the convergence probability and the integration of the subtour constraints directly into the optimization without using additional qubits by employing an approximation of exponential equality constraints. We believe that our results pave the way for effectively solving instances of VRP using quantum-based solutions, leveraging the space-efficient problem encoding and our initialization strategy, which limits the effect of barren-plateau under random parameter initialization.
item.dc:creator: Emanuele Casciaro, Mario De Simone, Stefano Martina, Fabio Mascherpa, Alfonso Amendola, Filippo Caruso

item.title: Bounds for lattice points in terms of volume and successive minima
item.description: arXiv:2610.41125v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove, in every dimension, the upper bound conjectured by Betke, Henk and Wills for the lattice-point enumerator in terms of volume and successive minima. For every convex body $K\subset R^n$ and full-rank lattice $\Lambda$, we establish $$ \#(K\cap\Lambda)\le\frac{\mathrm{vol}_n(K)}{\det\Lambda}\prod_{i=1}^n\left(1+\frac{i\lambda_i}{2}\right), $$ where $\lambda_i$ are the successive minima of $(K-K)/2$ with respect to $\Lambda$. Equality holds precisely for lattice translates of positive integral dilates of unimodular simplices. We also prove $$ \#(\mathrm{int}K\cap\Lambda)\ge\frac{\mathrm{vol}_n(K)}{\det\Lambda} \left(1-\frac{n}{4}\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}\lambda_i-\frac{n}{2}\lambda_n\right), $$ which implies the lower estimate with factor $1-\frac{1}{2}\sum_{i=1}^n i\lambda_i$. In dimension two we prove the lower bound with factor $(1-\lambda_1/2)(1-\lambda_2)$ when $\lambda_2\le1$. We also observe that a conjectured product lower bound for origin-symmetric bodies fails in dimension three. The proofs combine geometric compression, lattice-cell counts in coordinate sections, and an elementary coefficient comparison.
item.dc:creator: Jun Wang, Fei Xue

item.title: Traveling Salesman Problem on Graphs with Proportional Independent Set
item.description: arXiv:2610.41178v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give a deterministic algorithm for minimum-cost Hamiltonian cycle in undirected graphs with arbitrary real edge costs and an independent set of size at least $\alpha n$, for any fixed $3/7<\alpha\le1/2$. It runs in $O^*(\gamma(\alpha)^n)$ time for an explicit constant $\gamma(\alpha)<2$; for bipartite graphs, the bound is $O^*((1+2\sqrt2)^{n/2})\approx O^*(1.957^n)$. The algorithm is based on a restricted Held--Karp dynamic program. Its state enumeration uses structural properties of minimum-cost assignments arising from a regular triangulation of a product of simplices.
item.dc:creator: Ethan X. Fang, Shengtao Guo, Junwei Lu, Yuan Yao

item.title: A reciprocal Schoenberg inequality and its extensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.41325v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study reciprocal moments of the critical points of a polynomial with a simple zero at the origin. A positive similarity transforms a reciprocal derivative companion into a complex symmetric matrix. This gives a short proof of the reciprocal Schoenberg inequality and a refinement for every elementary symmetric function. We determine the optimal constants in the corresponding inequalities for every positive exponent, including the sublinear range, and extend the results to arbitrary positive charges. We also characterize the normal powers of the companion and of its symmetric representative. The resulting criterion gives the complete equality cases in two quartic inequalities and explains the appearance of noncollinear equality configurations at higher orders. We also obtain a closed generating determinant and a quantitative collinearity estimate.
item.dc:creator: Olga Holtz

item.title: List 3-Coloring in tame classes of graphs in quasipolynomial time
item.description: arXiv:2610.41620v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A class of graphs $\mathcal{G}$ is tame if there is a constant c such that every $n$-vertex graph in $\mathcal{G}$ has at most $n^c$ minimal separators. Many important graph classes are tame, including chordal graphs, permutation graphs, and circle graphs. Several fundamental problems, most notably Max Weight Independent Set, can be solved in polynomial time on every tame class, which explains in a unified way their tractability on all these classes. We show that List 3-Coloring can be solved in quasipolynomial time on every tame class of graphs.
item.dc:creator: Pawe{\l} Rz\k{a}\.zewski

item.title: Exchange graphs and $g$-vectors of surface rigid algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.41703v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We classify the connected components of support $\tau$-tilting graphs of surface rigid algebras associated with partial tagged triangulations of punctured marked surfaces with nonempty boundary. For a connected algebra, the graph is disconnected if and only if the algebra is weakly symmetric, has at least two simple modules, and has Cartan rank one. In this case, it has exactly two connected components. For every nonzero $\tau$-rigid pair over a connected surface rigid algebra, the graph of $\tau$-tilting completions is connected. More generally, we classify the completion components for an arbitrary surface rigid algebra and a fixed $\tau$-rigid pair. For partial tagged triangulations with all endpoints at punctures, we express the Cartan matrix and $g$-vectors by signed endpoint data. We prove that $\tau$-tilting finiteness is equivalent to positive definiteness of the Cartan matrix. In the finite case, we determine the primitive $g$-vector ray generators in endpoint coordinates. Trees give type A, and a criterion on the original partial tagged triangulation distinguishes types D and C in the unicyclic case.
item.dc:creator: Ping He, Bo Le

item.title: An extension of the classic Buneman theorem from phylogenetic trees to networks
item.description: arXiv:2610.41725v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Phylogenetic networks provide a natural framework for representing reticulate evolutionary events such as horizontal gene transfer and hybridization. In the present manuscript, we investigate the identifiability of phylogenetic networks under (hardwired) parsimony, a natural extension of Maximum Parsimony from trees to networks. More precisely, we ask which structural features of a network can be uniquely inferred from so-called $A_k$-alignments under this criterion. While identifiability has been studied extensively for phylogenetic trees under parsimony, little is known about the identifiability of networks under hardwired parsimony. We take a first step towards addressing this gap by developing a general framework for studying identifiability under hardwired parsimony. We then use this framework to show that the tree of blobs of a phylogenetic network can be reconstructed from its $A_1$-alignment. This result can be viewed as a natural extension of Buneman's well-known splits equivalence theorem. Finally, we show that, under hardwired parsimony, cycles of length at least $5$ cannot in general be uniquely identified from character data, establishing a fundamental limitation of hardwired parsimony.
item.dc:creator: Mirko Wilde, Mareike Fischer

item.title: Bethe Hessian Recovery through the Kesten-Stigum Regime
item.description: arXiv:2610.41802v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that outlier eigenvectors of the Bethe Hessian achieve weak recovery in the stochastic block model down to the Kesten-Stigum threshold, for every fixed common expected degree $d>1$. This extends previous recovery guarantees, which required $d$ to be sufficiently large. This threshold is information-theoretically optimal for the symmetric two-community model and is conjectured to mark the limit of efficient recovery in broader symmetric models. Our result matches the recovery guarantees of non-backtracking spectral methods while using Hermitian $n\times n$ matrices. To do this, we identify recursive formulas for the negative outlier eigenvalues and show that their eigenspaces have nonvanishing overlap with the corresponding planted eigenspaces. The proof constructs approximate eigenvectors from the planted labels on the limiting Poisson tree, with weights given by its Green's function, and transfers these approximations to the finite graph.
item.dc:creator: Dingding Dong, Theo McKenzie

item.title: Alcove walks, crystal structure and a Levi branching rule
item.description: arXiv:2610.41929v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In the Borel case $P=B$, we endow Haines' set of maximal-dimensional positively folded alcove walks (arXiv:2405.17174) with a crystal structure. We construct a bijection with the LS-gallery model of Gaussent and Littelmann (arXiv:math/0307122) and prove that it intertwines the root operators. This answers a question raised by Haines. We also extend the Gaussent-Littelmann stratification to the parabolic setting, prove the Levi branching rule for LS galleries, and compare the resulting gallery model with Haines' maximal-dimensional positively folded alcove walks in the parabolic setting.
item.dc:creator: Wenzhuo Wang

item.title: Treedepth is NP-Hard on Planar Graphs of Maximum Degree 3
item.description: arXiv:2610.42033v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Treedepth is an important parameter in algorithmic graph theory. It is known that the problem of computing the treedepth of a graph is NP-hard. It has been an open problem whether treedepth can be computed in polynomial time when the input graph is restricted to be planar, or of bounded degree. Assuming $P \neq NP$, we answer both questions in the negative: Under polynomial-time Turing reductions, it is NP-hard to compute the treedepth of planar graphs with maximum degree 3. This degree bound is best possible, since treedepth can be computed efficiently on graphs of maximum degree 2.
item.dc:creator: Kolja K\"uhn

item.title: Two choices suffice: $k$-out sampling leaves $O(n/k)$ intercomponent edges for $k\geq 2$
item.description: arXiv:2610.42067v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Given a simple undirected graph on $n$ vertices, random $k$-out sampling forms a spanning subgraph by having each vertex independently choose $k$ incident edges uniformly with replacement. We prove that, for every integer $k\geq2$, the expected number of original edges joining distinct sampled components is $O(n/k)$. This resolves the conjecture of Holm, King, Thorup, Zamir, and Zwick in its full range, improving their logarithmic sampling requirement to the optimal threshold of two choices per vertex. The bound fails for $k=1$, and the dependence $O(n/k)$ is tight up to constant factors. Our result holds with replacement and consequently also without replacement. In particular, this implies that contracting just two independent local choices per vertex suffices to reduce an arbitrary simple graph to a quotient with $O(n)$ edges in expectation, which is crucial in reducing the instance size for many contraction-based algorithms. Our proof uses switching arguments to relate intercomponent edges to bridges and a degree-weighted component potential, whose expectation we also bound with a switching argument.
item.dc:creator: Yanyu Chen, Yu Chen

item.title: Delocalized region of bipartite Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.42088v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider bipartite Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi graphs $\mathbb{G}(n, p, d/\sqrt{np})$ with two parts of sizes $n$ and $p$, respectively, and edge probability $d/\sqrt{pn}$. We show that for $d > b_* \log (n+p)$ all eigenvectors of its adjacency matrix, with eigenvalues away from zero, are delocalized with high probability. The threshold $b_*$ is an explicit function of the size ratio $n/p$ and optimal for eigenvector delocalization near the spectral edges. Our results extend to bulk eigenvectors down to the optimal threshold $d\geq \mathcal{D}\sqrt{\log (n+p)}$ for a constant $\mathcal D \geq 1$. In the supercritical scale $d \gg \log (n+p)$ we show that all eigenvectors are delocalized. Our results also hold for sparse rectangular random matrices with independent entries.
item.dc:creator: Johannes Alt, Serafina Wald

item.title: Band Random Graphs: Connectivity, Geometry, and Transport
item.description: arXiv:2610.42107v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $G(n,p,m)$ be the random subgraph of the cycle power $C_n^m$ obtained by retaining each edge independently with probability $p$. We study connectivity, component geometry, and random walks throughout the regime $\log n\ll m<n/2$. We prove that $p\sim(\log n)/(2m)$ is a sharp threshold for connectivity. If $n(1-p)^{2m}\to\lambda\in(0,\infty)$, then the number of isolated vertices converges to $\mathrm{Poisson}(\lambda)$, and with high probability every other vertex lies in a single component $C_1$. In particular, the connectivity probability converges to $e^{-\lambda}$. The component $C_1$ contains a cyclic chain of connected sets occupying all but an $o(1)$ fraction of each consecutive block of length $\asymp m$, with $\Theta(m\log n)$ edges between consecutive sets. Its diameter has order $n/m+\log n/\log\log n$ with high probability. For every fixed $c>1$, uniformly over $p\geq c\log n/(2m)$, the lazy-walk spectral gap is asymptotic in probability to that of $C_n^m$. In the same range, the mean hitting time of simple random walk satisfies, uniformly over distinct $x,y$, $$ H_G(x,y)=\frac{2|E(G)|}{d_G(y)} +\frac{r_{xy}(n-r_{xy})}{\kappa_m} +o_{\mathrm{Prob}}\left(n+\frac{n^2}{m^2}\right), $$ where $r_{xy}$ is cyclic distance between vertices $x$ and $y$, $d_G(z)$ is the degree of vertex $z$ and $\kappa_m=(m+1)(2m+1)/6$. Thus, for this random graph model, connectivity has the Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi asymptotics with $2m$ possible neighbours, while distances, relaxation, and hitting times retain the geometry of the underlying cycle.
item.dc:creator: Shantanav Chakraborty, Kyle Luh, Rudransh Pratap Singh

item.title: Abelianization and moment maps
item.description: arXiv:2610.42123v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: When $X_G=\mathbb{C}^n/\!/G$ is a GIT quotient of a vector space, replacing $G$ with a maximal torus $T \subset G$ produces a closely related toric variety $X_T:=\mathbb{C}^N/\!/T$, the \emph{Abelianization} of $X_G$. Abelian/non-Abelian correspondences connect structures on $X_G$ with structures on $X_T$. In this paper, we study the interaction between the toric moment map $\mu$ of $X_T$ and $X_G$, when $X_G=\mathrm{Gr}(r,n)$.
