We do this by looking at the restriction of $\mu$ to an intermediate space $Z/T \subset X_T$, where $Z/G=X_G$. We show that the generic fibres of this map are co-Lagrangians that project to Lagrangians on $X_G$. We completely describe the image in the case where $X_G=\mathrm{Gr}(2,n)$, and show that in the general $\mathrm{Gr}(r,n)$ case the image can be sliced so that each piece is determined by a finite set of points, related to matroid circuits.
item.dc:creator: Elana Kalashnikov, Ruxandra Moraru, Francisco Villacis

item.title: On kernel Mengerian orientations of line multigraphs
item.description: arXiv:1507.06053v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A kernel of a digraph is an independent set $K$ such that every vertex outside $K$ has an arc to a vertex in $K$. We present a polyhedral description of kernels in clique-acyclic orientations of line multigraphs. Given a digraph $D$, let $FK(D)$ denote its fractional kernel polytope, and let $\sigma(D)$ denote the linear system defining $FK(D)$. A digraph $D$ is called kernel perfect if every induced subdigraph has a kernel, called kernel ideal if the fractional kernel polytope of every induced subdigraph is integral, and called kernel Mengerian if the defining system of every induced subdigraph is totally dual integral. We show that a clique-acyclic orientation of a line multigraph is kernel ideal if and only if it is kernel Mengerian. These equivalent properties hold precisely when the orientation is kernel perfect and has no even-cycle obstruction.
item.dc:creator: Han Xiao

item.title: Asymptotics of principal evaluations of Schubert polynomials for layered permutations
item.description: arXiv:1805.04341v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Denote by $u(n)$ the largest principal specialization of the Schubert polynomial: $ u(n) := \max_{w \in S_n} \mathfrak{S}_w(1,\ldots,1) $ Stanley conjectured in [arXiv:1704.00851] that there is a limit $\lim_{n\to \infty} \, \frac{1}{n^2} \log u(n), $ and asked for a limiting description of permutations achieving the maximum $u(n)$. Merzon and Smirnov conjectured in [arXiv:1410.6857] that this maximum is achieved on layered permutations. We resolve both Stanley's problems restricted to layered permutations.
item.dc:creator: Alejandro H. Morales, Igor Pak, Greta Panova

item.title: A proof of Ryser's circulant Hadamard conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2302.08346v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that an $n\times n$ circulant Hadamard matrix must satisfy a family of congruence equations that have solutions only when $n \leq 4$, proving Ryser's 1963 conjecture that no such matrices exist for $n>4$.
item.dc:creator: Joshua Morris

item.title: NumPSLA -- An experimental research tool for pseudoline arrangements and order types
item.description: arXiv:2503.02336v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a program for enumerating all pseudoline arrangements with a small number of pseudolines and abstract order types of small point sets. This program supports computer experiments with these structures, and it complements the order-type database of Aichholzer, Aurenhammer, and Krasser. This system makes it practical to explore the abstract order types for 12 points, and the pseudoline arrangements of 11 pseudolines.
item.dc:creator: G\"unter Rote

item.title: On almost Gallai colourings in complete graphs
item.description: arXiv:2503.17334v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate a rainbow analogue of the Ruzsa--Szemer\'edi problem. For $t \in \mathbb{N}$, we say that a colouring of $E(K_n)$ is almost $t$-Gallai if no two rainbow $t$-cliques share an edge. Motivated by a lemma of Berkowitz on bounding the modulus of the characteristic function of clique counts in random graphs, we study the maximum number $\tau_t(n)$ of rainbow $t$-cliques in an almost $t$-Gallai colouring of $E(K_n)$. For every $t \ge 4$, we show that $n^{2-o(1)} \leq \tau_t(n) = o(n^2)$. For $t=3$, surprisingly, the behaviour is substantially different. Our main result establishes that $$\left ( \frac{1}{2}-o(1) \right ) n\log n \le \tau_3(n) \le O\big (n^{\sqrt{2}}\log n \big ),$$ which gives the first non-trivial improvements over the simple lower and upper bounds. Our proof combines various applications of the probabilistic method and a generalisation of the edge-isoperimetric inequality for the hypercube.
item.dc:creator: Alexandr Grebennikov, Let\'icia Mattos, Tibor Szab\'o

item.title: Coherent configurations and Frobenius structures
item.description: arXiv:2507.21774v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that coherent configurations can be represented as modules over Frobenius structures in the category of real nonnegative matrices. We generalize the notion of admissible morphism from association schemes to coherent configurations. We show that the Frobenius structure associated to a coherent configuration can be modified to become a dagger Frobenius structure, and use this to connect the coherent configurations to groupoids and $H^*$-algebras. We examine the properties of the dagger Frobenius structure with respect to admissible morphisms. We introduce the matrix $O$ obtained as the composition of comultiplication and multiplication of the dagger Frobenius structure and prove that we may obtain the valencies of colors, and thus recover the original coherent configuration, as an eigenvector of $O$. In the last part of the paper, we examine the spectrum of $O$ and apply it to generalize the Lagrange theorem from groups to association schemes.
item.dc:creator: Dominik Lachman, Gejza Jen\v{c}a, Anna Jen\v{c}ov\'a

item.title: Hamilton cycles in pseudorandom graphs: resilience and approximate decompositions
item.description: arXiv:2507.22807v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Dirac's classical theorem asserts that, for $n\ge 3$, any $n$-vertex graph with minimum degree at least $\frac{n}{2}$ is Hamiltonian. Furthermore, if we additionally assume that such graphs are regular and sufficiently large, then, by the breakthrough work of Csaba, K\"uhn, Lo, Osthus, and Treglown, they admit a decomposition into Hamilton cycles and at most one perfect matching, solving the well-known Nash-Williams conjecture. In the pseudorandom setting, it has long been conjectured that similar results hold in much sparser graphs. We prove two overarching theorems for graphs that exclude excessively dense subgraphs, which yield asymptotically optimal resilience and Hamilton-decomposition results in sparse pseudorandom graphs. Firstly, our results imply that for every fixed $\gamma>0$, there exists a constant $C>0$ such that if $G$ is a spanning subgraph of an $(n,d,\lambda)$-graph satisfying $\delta(G)\ge\bigl(\tfrac12+\gamma\bigr)d$ and $d/\lambda\ge C$, then $G$ must contain a Hamilton cycle. Secondly, we show that for every $\varepsilon>0$, there is $C>0$ so that any $(n,d,\lambda)$-graph $G$ with $d/\lambda\ge C$ contains at least $\bigl(1-\varepsilon\bigr)\tfrac d2$ edge-disjoint Hamilton cycles, and, finally, we prove that the entire edge set of $G$ can be covered by no more than $\bigl(1+\varepsilon\bigr)\tfrac d2$ such cycles. All bounds are asymptotically optimal and significantly improve earlier results on Hamiltonian resilience, packing, and covering in sparse pseudorandom graphs.
item.dc:creator: Nemanja Dragani\'c, Jaehoon Kim, Hyunwoo Lee, David Munh\'a Correia, Mat\'ias Pavez-Sign\'e, Benny Sudakov

item.title: Closed Colored Models and Demazure Crystals
item.description: arXiv:2512.05479v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct and study solvable lattice models whose partition functions are Demazure characters. Two types of colored generalizations of the five-vertex model can be defined that are called the open and closed models. States of both models are associated with Gelfand-Tsetlin patterns, or equivalently, semistandard Young tableaux. We characterize the tableaux arising from states of the closed model and prove that they form a Demazure crystal. This is stronger than identifying the partition function as a Demazure character: it requires constructing Kashiwara crystal operators on the states through lattice moves and recoloring. For the open model, Brubaker, Bump, Buciumas, and Gustafsson showed that the states realize (crystal) Demazure atoms. We also give a new, independent proof of their result. Bump and Naprienko considered bosonic models involving a parameter t. In these models, the edges and vertices are constructed by fusion of simpler edge and vertex types. Taking t=0 produces bosonic analogs of the open model. By reversing the fusion order, we construct closed bosonic models and establish their Yang-Baxter equations, yielding a Demazure-Lusztig recursion for the partition functions. At t=0, these models specialize to bosonic analogues of the closed five-vertex model, and we prove that their states form Demazure crystals.
item.dc:creator: Yingzi Yang

item.title: Tight paths in fully directed hypergraphs
item.description: arXiv:2601.00144v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: It is well-known that every tournament has a spanning path. We consider hypergraph analogues. In an \emph{$r$-uniform fully directed hypergraph}, or \emph{$r$-digraph}, every edge is a list or $r$ distinct vertices. An $(r,k)$-tournament is an $r$-digraph $G$ such that for every $r$-set $S$ of vertices in $G$, exactly $k$ of the orderings of $S$ are edges in $G$. A \emph{directed tight path} is an $r$-digraph $G$ whose vertices can be ordered so that the intervals of size $r$ are the edges in $G$. Let $f(n,r,k)$ be the maximum $s$ such that every $n$-vertex $(r,k)$-tournament contains a tight path on $s$ vertices. Since every tournament has a spanning path, we have $f(n,2,1)=n$. In this paper, we show that the minimum $k$ such that $f(n,r,k)$ tends to infinity with $n$ is in the interval $\left[\left(1-\frac{1}{r}-O(\frac{\log r}{r^2\log\log r})\right)r!, ~\left(1-\frac{1}{r} - \frac{\varphi(r)-1}{r!}\right)r!\right]$ where $\varphi(r)$ is the Euler Totient Function, and we find the exact value when $r\le 5$. We also show that $\Omega(\sqrt{\log n/\log \log n}) \le f(n,3,3) \le O(\log n)$ and $f(n,3,4)\ge \Omega(n^{1/5})$.
item.dc:creator: Richard C. Devine, Kevin G. Milans

item.title: Decomposable shuffles
item.description: arXiv:2602.00461v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a combinatorial and order-theoretic framework for shuffles, understood as ordered partitions of the natural numbers. We introduce decomposable shuffles as generalised sums of finite ordinals, copies of $\omega$, and copies of its dual $\omega^*$, indexed by countable scattered linear orders. These building blocks are called benches, ladders and snakes, respectively. We introduce a subclass, layered shuffles, and for this subclass we construct an explicit finite-address representation which reduces comparison in the induced order on $\mathbb N$ to lexicographic comparison of integer tuples. We determine the order types of represented layered shuffles, establish that all represented orders are scattered, and define an involution that realises order duality. Finally, we introduce a hierarchical composition on bench-free injective uniform shuffles of fixed sign. For each sign, this operation yields a monoid graded by reduced degree. Its degree-one component is isomorphic to $\operatorname{Sym}(\mathbb N)$ and consists precisely of the invertible elements.
item.dc:creator: Jo\~ao Dias, Bruno Dinis, Carlos Correia Ramos

item.title: Characterizing the optimum bases of a convex geometry using quasi-closed hypergraphs
item.description: arXiv:2603.14615v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Optimizing an implicational base of a closure system consists in turning this implicational base into an equivalent one with premises and conclusions as small as possible. This task is known to be hard in general but tractable for a number of classes of closure systems. In particular, several classes of convex geometries are known to have tractable optimization, while the problem was recently claimed to remain hard in general convex geometries. Continuing this line of research, we give a characterization of the optimum bases of a convex geometry in terms of what we call quasi-closed hypergraphs. We then use this characterization to show that when each quasi-closed hypergraph has disjoint edges, any implicational base of the convex geometry can be optimized in polynomial time with existing minimization and reduction algorithms. Finally, we prove that this property applies to double-shelling convex geometries, $D$-geometries, convex geometries with the $n$-Carousel property and $q$-acceptant convex geometries, thus unifying and extending the existing results regarding the tractability of optimization.
item.dc:creator: Anthony Meunier, Lhouari Nourine, Simon Vilmin

item.title: Bounded Bruhat intervals and affine Coxeter groups
item.description: arXiv:2606.16894v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Dyer (1991) proved that, for each fixed length $k$, only finitely many isomorphism types of Bruhat intervals occur in finite Coxeter groups. In this short paper, we prove that this result holds also for affine Coxeter groups, and moreover that this characterizes the affine groups among all infinite Coxeter groups. We also show that the coefficients of $q$ in the Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials of a Coxeter group are bounded if and only if the group is finite or affine.
item.dc:creator: Grant T. Barkley, Christian Gaetz

item.title: A characterization of edge-chromatic 3-critical graphs
item.description: arXiv:2606.27131v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A graph with maximum degree $\Delta$ is \emph{$\Delta$-critical} if it is connected, has chromatic index $\Delta+1$, and the deletion of any edge reduces its chromatic index to $\Delta$; it is \emph{nontrivial} if it has no subgraph $H$ with $|E(H)|>\Delta\lfloor |V(H)|/2\rfloor$. We prove a characterization of all nontrivial $3$-critical graphs: every such graph is obtained either from smaller $3$-critical graphs by replacing a vertex with a triangle, by a Haj\'os-join, or by replacing a vertex with a suitable class~$1$ graph, or from a snark by deleting at most one vertex and some independent edges. The third operation, which we call a Meredith-type extension, generalizes the Meredith extension by allowing other class~$1$ graphs in place of $K_{2,3}$, and we give a sufficient condition under which it produces new nontrivial $3$-critical graphs from smaller ones. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first characterization of this kind for edge-chromatic $3$-critical graphs, and the Meredith-type extension has not previously been considered in this generality. The characterization was found by analyzing the output of an exhaustive computer search for nontrivial $3$-critical graphs of orders $13$ to $24$, and we make the resulting data publicly available. Based on these data, we also propose two conjectures that are closely related to the case $\Delta=3$ of Seymour's exact conjecture and to Gr\"otzsch's conjecture on the $3$-edge-colorability of planar graphs.
item.dc:creator: Le Chen, Songling Shan

item.title: Combinatorial identities derived from explicit formulas of Gauss hypergeometric functions
item.description: arXiv:2607.10643v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In the present paper, with the help of the Fa\`a di Bruno formula and several identities of partial Bell polynomials, the author establishes explicit formulas of the Gauss hypergeometric functions \begin{gather*} {\,}_2F_1\biggl(\frac{1-n}{2},\frac{2-n}{2};\frac{3}{2}-m;z^2\biggr), \quad {\,}_2F_1\biggl(-\frac{n}{2},\frac{1-n}{2};\frac{1}{2}-m;z^2\biggr),\\ {\,}_2F_1\biggl(a,a+\frac{1}{2};\frac{3}{2}-m;z^2\biggr), \quad {\,}_2F_1\biggl(a,a+\frac{1}{2};\frac{1}{2}-m;z^2\biggr) \end{gather*} for $m,n\in\mathbb{N}$ and $a\in\mathbb{C}$, and then derives two combinatorial identities \begin{equation*} \sum_{k=0}^{m}\frac{2^k}{k!} \binom{2m-2k}{m-k} \sum_{\ell=0}^{k} \frac{(-1)^\ell}{2^\ell} \frac{(2k-2\ell-1)!!}{(n-\ell)!} \binom{2k-\ell-1}{\ell-1} =\frac{1}{n!}\binom{2m-n}{m} \end{equation*} and \begin{equation*} \sum_{k=1}^{m}\frac{1}{(k!)^2}\binom{2m-2k}{m-k} \sum_{\ell=1}^{k} \binom{k}{\ell}\ell(2k-\ell-1)! (2a)_\ell =\binom{2m+2a}{m}-\binom{2m}{m}, \end{equation*} where $m\in\mathbb{N}_0$, $n\in\mathbb{Z}$, and $a\in\mathbb{C}$. These newly-established identities extend and generalize the beautiful combinatorial identity \begin{equation*} \sum_{k=0}^{n} \frac{2^{k}}{k!}\binom{2n-2k}{n-k} \sum_{j=0}^{k}\frac{(-1)^{j}}{2^j} \frac{(2k-2j-1)!!}{(n-j)!} \binom{2k-j-1}{j-1} =\frac{1}{n!}, \quad n\in\mathbb{N}_0, \end{equation*} which was obtained in Theorem 4 of the paper "F. Qi, C.-Y. He, and D. Lim, Explicit formulas of two Gauss hypergeometric functions and several combinatorial identities, Discrete Appl. Math. Vol. 393 (2026), 215--229. DOI: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.dam.2026.06.023."
item.dc:creator: Feng Qi

item.title: On the Column Number of Delta-Modular Matrices: an $O(m^2 \Delta)$ Bound via the Shifted Heller Constant
item.description: arXiv:2608.06215v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we build on the analysis initiated by Averkov and Schymura (2022) and prove that the shifted Heller constant for matrices with $m$ rows is at most $m^2 + m$ for all sufficiently large $m$. Consequently, the number of distinct columns of a $\Delta$-modular matrix $A \in Z^{m \times n}$ of rank $m$ is at most $O(m^2 \Delta)$. This improves upon the earlier bounds of $O(m^4 \Delta)$ and $O(m^2 \Delta^2)$.
item.dc:creator: Elizaveta Pribytkova, Dmitrii Gribanov, Dmitrii Taletskii, Stanislav Moiseev

item.title: The minimum of the graph likelihood
item.description: arXiv:2608.19467v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The likelihood of a finite simple undirected graph $G$ on $n$ vertices is the probability that the uniform sequential attachment process, which at each step joins a new vertex to a uniformly random subset of uniformly random size of the vertices already present, outputs a graph isomorphic to $G$. Dervovic, Mocherla and Severini conjectured that the likelihood is minimised by the balanced complete bipartite graph. We prove that, among complete bipartite graphs of a given order, the balanced one uniquely minimises the likelihood. Exact computation shows that it also minimises over all graphs for every order from $6$ through $14$. At $n=15$, the exact global minimisers are $C_5[\bar K_3]$ and its complement, giving the first counterexample. Completed exact searches show that the global minimisers at order $16$ are $K_{8,8}$ and its complement. At order $17$, the unique minimiser is a self-complementary mixed blow-up of $C_5$. At order $18$, the minimisers are $K_{9,9}$ and its complement. We show that the failure is not sporadic by proving that the likelihood of the balanced complete bipartite graph is $2^{-(1/2-1/(8\ln 2)+o(1))n^2}$, whereas the minimum over all graphs of order $n$ is $2^{-(1/2+o(1))n^2}$, so the conjectured minimiser exceeds the minimum by a factor exponential in $n^2$. We also determine the Shannon entropy of the process to leading order, namely $n^2/(4\ln 2)$ bits, which shows that the conjectured minimiser is in fact more likely than a typical output of the process. The proofs rest on a vertex deletion recurrence which evaluates the likelihood in time $O(2^n n)$ and which closes on the blow-ups of any fixed base graph.
item.dc:creator: Simone Severini, Eric W. Weisstein

item.title: Ramanujan Transforms and Maximum Energy of Odd-Total-Exponent Integral Circulants
item.description: arXiv:2608.29523v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a finite graph, its energy is the sum of the absolute values of its adjacency eigenvalues. Let n be the product of powers of distinct odd primes, where all exponents are positive integers, the sum of the exponents is odd, and every prime whose exponent is odd is at least five. Among all nonempty sets of proper divisors of n, the energy of the corresponding integral circulant graph is uniquely maximised by the checkerboard divisor set consisting of those divisors for which the sum of the prime-power exponents is even. The maximum energy is one half of the sum of n and the product, over all prime factors, of explicit polynomial quantities. For exponent k and parameter x, the corresponding polynomial is given by two k plus one times x to the k-th power, together with four times the sum from zero to k minus one of j plus one times x to the j-th power with alternating sign determined by the parity of k minus j. For the proof, we use weighted prime-power Ramanujan transforms, which give an exact energy model in tensor form and extend to a polynomial matrix family for real parameters greater than one. A semidefinite parity theorem shows that the matrix obtained from this polynomial family by an explicit positive diagonal normalisation is a real symmetric contraction whose unique eigenvalue of modulus one is the simple eigenvalue determined by the parity of the exponent; this holds for even exponents at least two and parameters at least three, and for odd exponents at least one and parameters at least five. Tensorising this spectral structure and centring the binary divisor tensor yield a sharp one-norm bound for the corresponding tensor operator on sign vectors. In particular, for n equal to p squared times q cubed, with distinct odd primes p and q and with q at least five, this proves Roldan's conjectured maximality in this range.
item.dc:creator: Jianwei Jiang, Chunhua Yang

item.title: Local Fan-type obstructions and Ore-type conditions for rainbow Hamiltonicity in graph systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.13977v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $G=(G_1,...,G_n)$ be a graph system on a common $n$-vertex set $V$. For $v\in V$, set \[ \delta(v)=\min_{i\in[n]}d_{G_i}(v), \qquad E_{\cap}=\bigcap_{i=1}^n E(G_i), \] and let $d^c(u,v)$ denote the length of a shortest rainbow $u$--$v$ path. We study Hamiltonicity conditions imposed only on pairs at small rainbow distance. Suppose that every $G_i$ is $2$-connected and that \[ \delta(u),\delta(v)<\frac n2, \qquad d^c(u,v)\le2 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad uv\in E_{\cap}. \] Our main result shows that any system satisfying this local Fan-type condition but containing no rainbow Hamilton cycle must satisfy \[ E_{\cap}=\varnothing, \qquad \sum_{v\in V}\delta(v)\le\frac{n^2-1}{2}. \] Consequently, either $E_{\cap}\ne\varnothing$ or $\sum_{v\in V}\delta(v)\ge\lceil n^2/2\rceil$ guarantees a rainbow Hamilton cycle. We further prove that the local Ore-type condition \[ \delta(u)+\delta(v)<n, \qquad d^c(u,v)\le2 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad uv\in E_{\cap} \] already forces a rainbow Hamilton cycle. Along the way, the Fan-type hypothesis yields a rainbow Hamilton path and a rainbow $(n-1)$-cycle. For diagonal systems, our conditions reduce to the classical Fan and local Ore conditions. The proofs combine rainbow rotation--extension with a double-counting argument in an auxiliary digraph. Keywords: graph system; rainbow Hamilton cycle; rainbow distance; Fan-type condition; Ore-type condition; rotation--extension.
item.dc:creator: Ailian Chen, Hao Chen

item.title: Triangulation, Volume, and Symmetries of a Dihedral Group Analogue of the Permutohedron
item.description: arXiv:2610.28672v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study an analogue of the permutohedron for the dihedral group, which we call the dihedral permutohedron. We determine the facet structure of the dihedral permutohedron, use the facet structure to construct a triangulation, and determine a nice combinatorial formula for the volume of the dihedral permutohedron. Lastly, we find a family of interesting unimodular affine symmetries of the odd dihedral permutohedron.
item.dc:creator: Colin Olairez

item.title: Prime Nullspace Matrices and Even Dominating Sets
item.description: arXiv:2610.31475v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A non-zero $m \times n$ (0, 1)-matrix $A$ is called a {\em nullspace matrix} if each entry $(i, j)$ of $A$ has an even number of $1's$ in the set of entries consisting of $(i, j)$ and its rectilinear neighbors. These matrices correspond to even dominating sets of $m \times n$ grid graphs. We study these matrices and consider those that cannot be constructed from smaller nullspace matrices.
item.dc:creator: William F. Klostermeyer

item.title: A proof of Wang's planar $D$-coloring conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.33322v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove Wang's planar $D$-coloring conjecture. A $D$-coloring of a graph is a proper edge coloring in which every subgraph isomorphic to $K_4$ minus an edge is rainbow. Wang conjectured that every planar graph of maximum degree $\Delta$ has a $D$-coloring with $9$ colors if $\Delta=4$, $10$ colors if $\Delta=5$, and $2\Delta-1$ colors if $\Delta\ge6$. Hu, Kong and Wang proved the cases $\Delta\le5$ and $\Delta\ge33$. We prove the sharp bound $2\Delta-1$ for every $\Delta\ge6$, settling the remaining cases. The proof uses discharging; the case $\Delta=6$ is computer-assisted.
item.dc:creator: Harshit Verma

item.title: EKR Results for Cuspidal Representations of $\mathrm{GL}_2(q)$
item.description: arXiv:2610.38472v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\mathcal{S}_\chi$ be a cuspidal representation of $\mathrm{GL}_2(q)$. A subset $S \subseteq \mathrm{GL}_2(q)$ is {$t$-intersecting} if $\dim_{\mathbb{C}}\{v \in \mathcal{S}_\chi: g_1v = g_2v\} \geqslant t$ for any $g_1, g_2 \in S$. In this paper, we determine $\max{|S|}$ where $S$ is $t$-intersecting.
item.dc:creator: Jiaqi Liao

item.title: Site Percolation on Multi-dimensional Lattice
item.description: arXiv:1307.2827v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Sites in an infinite d-dimensional lattice, open with probability greater or equal to 1/d, form an infinite open path.
item.dc:creator: Marko Puljic

item.title: Small measure expansion in connected noncompact groups
item.description: arXiv:2111.05236v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Assuming $G$ is unimodular and $K>1$, and that $\mu(A^2) < K \mu(A)$. We show that this is a continuous surjective group homomorphism $\chi: G \to L$ with a compact kernel, where $L$ is a Lie group satisfying $$\dim(L) \leq \lfloor\log K\rfloor(\lfloor\log K\rfloor+1)/2.$$ This dimension bound is sharp, We also establish the relationship between $A$ and its image under the quotient map, and obtain a more general version of this result for the product set $AB$ without assuming unimodularity. We present two applications: (1) An inverse Kemperman theorem in noncompact groups. Let $G$ be a connected, noncompact, locally compact group with a left Haar measure $\mu$, and let $A$ and $B$ be nonempty, compact subsets of $G$. We classify all cases where $G$, $A$, and $B$ exhibit nearly minimal expansion properties (in the unimodular case, this means $\mu(AB)$ is close to $\mu(A) + \mu(B)$). This result completes the noncompact cases of the Kemperman inverse problem and resolves a question posed by Griesmer and Tao. (2) An effective generalized Margulis lemma for discrete subgroups of almost-connected locally compact groups acting properly by isometries. If $B(x,4r)$ can be covered by $K$ translates of $B(x,r)$ at one point and one scale, it gives a small radius $r/2M$, and the group generated at this radius has a subgroup of index at most $M \exp((\log K)^4)$ which is nilpotent modulo a finite normal subgroup. The nilpotency step is bounded by $(\log K)^2$, and \[ M\leq K^{\exp(C(\log K)^4\log\log K)} \] and $C$ is an absolute constant.
item.dc:creator: Jinpeng An, Yifan Jing, Chieu-Minh Tran, Ruixiang Zhang

item.title: Profile and neighbourhood complexity of graphs excluding a minor and tree-structured graphs
item.description: arXiv:2501.08895v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The \emph{$r$-neighbourhood complexity} of a graph $G$ is the function counting, for a given integer $k$, the largest possible number, over all vertex-subsets $A$ of size $k$, of subsets of $A$ realized as the intersection between the $r$-neighbourhood of some vertex and $A$. A~refinement of this notion is the \emph{$r$-profile complexity}, that counts the maximum number of distinct distance-vectors from any vertex to the vertices of $A$, ignoring distances larger than~$r$. Typically, in structured graph classes such as graphs of bounded VC-dimension or chordal graphs, these functions are bounded, leading to insights into their structural properties and efficient algorithms. We improve existing bounds on the $r$-profile complexity (and thus on the $r$-neighbourhood complexity) for graphs in several structured graph classes. We show that the $r$-profile complexity of graphs excluding $K_h$ as a minor is in $O_h(r^{3h-3}k)$. For graphs of treewidth at most~$t$, we give a bound in $O_t(r^{t+1}k)$, which is tight up to a function of~$t$ as a factor. These bounds improve results of Joret and Rambaud and answer a question of their paper [Combinatorica, 2024]. We also apply our methods to other classes of bounded expansion such as graphs excluding a fixed complete graph as a subdivision. For outerplanar graphs, we can improve our treewidth bound by a factor of $r$ and conjecture that a similar improvement holds for graphs with bounded simple treewidth. For graphs of treelength at most~$\ell$, we give the upper bound of $O(k(r^2(\ell+1)^k))$, which we improve to $O\left (k\cdot (r 2^k + r^2k^2) \right)$ in the case of chordal graphs and $O(k^2r)$ for interval graphs. Our bounds also imply relations between the order, diameter and metric dimension of graphs in these classes, improving results from [Beaudou et al., SIDMA 2017].
item.dc:creator: Laurent Beaudou, Jan Bok, Florent Foucaud, Daniel A. Quiroz, Jean-Florent Raymond

item.title: Tackling the 6/49 Lottery and Debunking Common Myths with Probabilistic Methods and Combinatorial Designs
item.description: arXiv:2603.24170v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: At the end, the house always wins! This simple truth holds for all public games of chance. Nevertheless, since lotteries have existed, people have tried everything to give luck a helping hand. This article compares objective scientific approaches to tackle the 6/49 lottery: probabilistic methods and combinatorial designs. The mathematical models developed herein can be modified and applied to other lotteries. The newly constructed (49, 6, 5) covering design is introduced, which meets the Sch\"onheim bound. For lottery designs and for covering designs, a benchmark based on probabilistic methods is presented. It is demonstrated that common attempts to outwit the odds correspond to limitations of numbers to subsets, which disproportionately reduce the chances of winning.
item.dc:creator: Ralph St\"ommer

item.title: Strongly Primitive Salem Growth Polynomials for Right-Angled Coxeter Groups
item.description: arXiv:2606.29397v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study standard spherical growth rates of right-angled Coxeter groups through the clique polynomial of the defining graph. We prove that every even degree at least four occurs as the degree of a strongly primitive Salem growth rate: for each $d\geq2$, there are infinitely many connected $K_{2d+1}$-free defining graphs whose full reciprocal-radius polynomial is an irreducible Salem polynomial of degree $2d$. We also establish independence-polynomial obstructions for prescribed Salem polynomials, including a sharp first-coefficient bound $a_1\leq-5$. Finally, an elementary golden-ratio growth gap excludes Lehmer's number from the standard spherical growth rates of right-angled Coxeter groups.
item.dc:creator: Mingyu Oh

item.title: Heilbronn's Problem in the Unit Triangle: Computational Optimality Certificates for $n \le 8$
item.description: arXiv:2607.15021v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study Heilbronn's triangle problem in the unit right triangle, where $n$ points are placed to maximize the smallest of the $\binom{n}{3}$ triangle areas they span. We prove a boundary-structure result: unless all three vertices are occupied, some optimal configuration with $n \ge 5$ has at least four points on the boundary, one edge containing two of them. With the affine $S_3$ symmetry this fixes four boundary points and $n$ orientation variables in a mixed-integer model that certifies global optimality for all $n \le 8$ up to a relative gap of $10^{-4}$. For $n \le 7$ this independently confirms the known exact optima, the case $n = 7$ having been proved by Zeng and Chen with symbolic computation. For $n = 8$, where only bounds were known, it narrows the gap to Cantrell's configuration fourfold in 39 minutes on one machine. The optimum there is conjectured to be the real root of a septic obtained by Chen, Zeng and Zhou, which our reconstruction confirms to 250 digits. We show its Galois group is $S_7$, so on that conjecture no expression in radicals exists.
item.dc:creator: Nathan Sudermann-Merx

item.title: A Sharp Refinement of Samuels' Inequality via Cap Moves
item.description: arXiv:2608.22816v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $0\le \mu_1\le \mu_2 \le \cdots \le \mu_n$ and $\delta > 0$. Samuels' conjecture states that if $X_1,\dots,X_n$ are independent non-negative random variables with $\mathbb{E}[X_i] = \mu_i$, then $$ \mathbb{P}\left( \sum_{i=1}^n X_i < \delta + \sum_{i=1}^n \mu_i \right) \ge \min_{1\le i\le n} \prod_{j=i}^n \left(1-\frac{\mu_j}{\delta + \sum_{k=i}^n \mu_k}\right).$$ This conjecture was recently proved by Ling. In this note, we prove a refinement of Samuels' inequality via an operation called the \emph{cap move}. Our refined inequality is sharp, with equality attained for a strictly larger class of distributions than in the original inequality.
item.dc:creator: Yanjun Han, Zipei Nie

item.title: Mutually touching cylinders: Littlewood's seven, and at most ten in general
item.description: arXiv:2610.26940v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We give a computer-assisted proof that at most seven congruent infinite circular cylinders in $\mathbb{R}^3$ can touch pairwise. This answers a question of Littlewood from 1968. For cylinders of arbitrary radii we prove the upper bound ten. Whether ten can be attained remains open.
item.dc:creator: Kenta Kitamura, Ivan Mati\'c, Rado\v{s} Radoi\v{c}i\'c, Andreas Spomer

item.title: The geometric combinatorics of $k$-shuffle braid groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.28986v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper is the first in a series of two which aims at introducing a new family of groups called $k$-shuffle braid groups, denoted $\mathcal{B}_{n}(k)$. These groups have two intrinsically related stories. They were first observed by Calegari in arXiv:2105.11265 by looking at spaces of complex monic polynomials of degree $n$ whose critical values lie in $\mathbb{C} \setminus \{1, e^{\frac{2\pi i}{k}}, \dots, e^{\frac{2\pi i (k-1)}{k}}\}$. The $k$-shuffle braid groups are the fundamental groups of those spaces, which correspond geometrically to complements of $k$ translates of the discriminant variety. The second story starts from the poset of $k$-shuffle partitions, which were introduced by Drew Armstrong and explored in depth in his thesis arXiv:math/0611106. In this paper, we focus on the combinatorial aspects of $k$-shuffle braid groups starting from the poset of $k$-shuffle non-crossing partitions. We build a CW-complex on which the groups act freely, properly discontinuously and cocompactly, which we show is CAT(0) for dimension up to 7. For higher dimension, we show that the CAT(0) property is implied by the conjecture of Brady and McCammond that the dual braid complex is CAT(0) (arXiv:0909.4778).
item.dc:creator: Chlo\'e Postel-Vinay

item.title: Closing All-Exp Gaps in Local Search for the Traveling Salesman Problem and Maximum Constraint Assignment
item.description: arXiv:2610.31513v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove the all-exp property for the Traveling Salesman Problem with the $2$-opt neighborhood, and for $(3,2,2)$- and $(2,3,2)$-Maximum Constraint Assignment with the flip neighborhood. The all-exp property states that infinitely many instances have an initial solution from which every sequence of improving moves to a local optimum, and hence every run of local search, has exponential length. For the Traveling Salesman Problem, the all-exp property was previously known for every $k$-opt neighborhood with $k \ge 3$, so our result for $2$-opt completes the picture for all $k$-kopt neighborhoods. In $(p,q,r)$-Maximum Constraint Assignment, each constraint involves at most $p$ variables, each variable occurs in at most $q$ constraints, and each domain has size $r$. Decreasing any of the parameters of $(3,2,2)$ or $(2,3,2)$ yields a problem in which every sequence of improving flips has polynomial length, so both Maximum Constraint Assignment results are tight. All three results settle long-standing open problems. Our proofs build on a common construction idea, which reveals a close connection between the local-search dynamics of the three problems.
item.dc:creator: Sophia Heimann, Hung P. Hoang, Stefan Hougardy

item.title: The View-Obstruction Problem for Spheres in Dimensions Six and Seven
item.description: arXiv:2610.37711v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Place closed Euclidean balls of radius r at the points of (1/2, 1/2, ..., 1/2) + Z^n. The view-obstruction problem for spheres asks for the least r such that every ray from the origin into the open positive orthant meets a ball. Equivalently, it asks for D_n = sup_v min_{t in R} sum_i ||t v_i - 1/2||{Z}^2 over positive integer vectors v, where ||x||{Z} denotes the distance from x to the nearest integer. The values for n <= 5 are classical. We prove D_6 = 107/312, attained only by permutations of (12, 9, 7, 5, 3, 2), and D_7 = 73/180, attained only by permutations of (11, 10, 8, 7, 4, 3, 1). The proof reduces the supremum to a finite search. The key facts are an exact lower bound d_n(v) >= delta^2_U for every rational subspace U perpendicular to v, a matching fiber upper bound, and Banaszczyk's transference theorem, applied along the Korkine-Zolotarev flag of the dual lattice v^perpendicular intersection Z^n. The search is quotiented by signed coordinate permutations and carried out entirely in exact rational arithmetic. It terminates with a certificate: no node of the search is left unresolved, and every surviving candidate is evaluated exactly. The method also recovers the known values for n = 3, 4, 5.
item.dc:creator: Vineet Kahlon
